lens: Skeptical CNCF-ecosystem veteran: refute differentiation and adoption (what exists, what ships in 12 months, why platform teams and the two personas would not adopt)
verdict: The differentiation survives the attack: nothing shipping today combines a portable signed snapshot of a cluster's admission posture, the whole apiserver-shaped chain run offline with per-finding fidelity, a two-persona contract, and a PR onto the branch Argo/Flux already watch (competitors brief "What nobody does"; report §8), and my live checks this week found nothing that closes it — ConfigHub moved further from Git (OCI-pull only, cub-scout #505), Flux Schema is still CRD/CEL-only, Kargo OSS still has no validation step, KEP-5073 still does not publish native rules to OpenAPI. What the design under-credits is how much of the *engine* half is already commodity (Kyverno's `podSecurity` rule runs the k8s PSA library offline via the CLI; the Kyverno Playground backend already loads cluster resources, VAP bindings, exceptions and CRDs from a live cluster), so the durable moat is the snapshot format, quota/RBAC/inventory arithmetic, the contract, and the PR writer — not policy evaluation. The real risk is adoption, not uniqueness: the "zero developer cooperation" first hour as written needs a ClusterRole that reads every Secret's contents, an OCI registry with push rights, and a signing identity before the first finding appears; layer discovery assumes an Argo/Flux CR that the owner's own "deployed via pipeline" customers may not have; the digest-must-match-trailer and maxAge gates fail PRs for reasons unrelated to the change (the Monokle friction lesson moved inside the push path); two promotion-hook integrations presuppose a server the design forbids; and the `$vocabulary` trick in the contract is a spec no-op. None of this is fatal — each is a section change — but together they are the difference between the bot being required in branch protection and being removed after the second false failure.

findings.section: §3.5 Snapshot format (inventory/ layer) and §1.3 first-hour path; §0 item 7
findings.claim_or_choice: The inventory layer stores Secret/ConfigMap 'names+keys only' and `zhi snapshot rbac` emits a minimal ClusterRole a bank's security team can review; the consultant's first hour needs 'zero developer cooperation'.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Secret keys live in `.data`; the Kubernetes API has no names+keys projection (PartialObjectMetadata returns metadata only), so enumerating keys means the importer reads every Secret's contents cluster-wide, and the RBAC needed (`list`/`get secrets`) is exactly the grant regulated customers refuse to a consultant's laptop tool. When the layer degrades, the `secret-key` picker, ESO store-presence check and failure class 10 silently disappear for the customers the deployer persona is built for, and the 'reviewable ClusterRole' becomes the reason the tool is not approved.
findings.evidence: Design §3.5 `inventory/ names+keys only … [full]` and `rbac/`; report §5.1 item 10 ('names and keys (never values)') glosses that keys require reading the object; report §3.1 class 10; persona lens advice 2 as cited in design §1.3. Kubernetes list semantics (full objects; metadata-only via PartialObjectMetadataList still requires the `list` verb on secrets).
findings.suggested_fix: Default the inventory layer to names-only via the metadata client; make key enumeration an opt-in, namespace-scoped Role limited to workspace namespaces; prefer `ExternalSecret`/`SecretStore` status as evidence of key existence where ESO is present; have `zhi snapshot rbac` print 'this rule reads Secret contents' next to the rule; add 'import with namespace-scoped Roles only' as a supported degraded mode in S8's pass criterion.

findings.section: §0 item 7, §3.5 (OCI default, cosign v3, committed dir as air-gap exception), §1.3
findings.claim_or_choice: Snapshots default to an OCI artifact signed with cosign v3, 'never cut'; the committed directory is only the air-gap exception.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The first-hour path now requires, before any finding: approved cluster RBAC, an OCI registry reachable from the customer network with push rights, registry auth for every teammate, and a signing identity the design never assigns (keyless needs Fulcio/Rekor egress from the customer network; key-based needs key custody). That inverts the Datree post-mortem ('snapshot and rules must be local files in Git; hosted registry optional') and reintroduces the SaaS-style dependency that killed it, just with a registry instead of a service.
findings.evidence: Competitors brief Task C, Datree row ('Core value … lived in SaaS … Snapshot and rules must be local files in Git; hosted registry optional'); design §0 item 7 and §3.5 'verified by exec'ing a digest-pinned cosign'; §13 minimalist rejected for committed snapshots (bloat/border leakage) — the OCI default trades bloat for prerequisites.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the first hour a local, unsigned snapshot in `.zhi/cache/` (gitignored) or a tarball that `zhi validate` and `zhi ui` accept with an 'unsigned local snapshot' badge in the report header; make OCI+cosign the *sharing/refresh* tier that `zhi check` requires only to clear Blocking; name the signer (platform refresh job identity vs consultant keyless) and the offline key-based fallback explicitly.

findings.section: §5.1 Discovery; §3.1 `internal/layout/{argo,flux}`; §2.2 Environment entity
findings.claim_or_choice: `internal/layout` 'never asks where values live; it reads what the controllers read' — Argo, Flux, Kargo CRs (Compose phase 2).
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The owner's own framing is 'pushed into Git repositories and then deployed via pipeline'. A customer running `helm upgrade --install -f values-<env>.yaml` from GitLab CI, Helmfile, or Rancher Fleet has no Argo/Flux CR in the repo; discovery finds no layers and the consultant cannot use zhi at exactly the customers that lack a controller. The report shows validation today is 'almost entirely CI bolt-ons' and lists Helmfile as a live layering mechanism, yet the design has no reader for it and no manual layer declaration.
findings.evidence: Report §2 ('Where validation happens today. Almost entirely CI bolt-ons…'); report §4.7 Helmfile v1.7.4 row ('Per-env values + precedence lists'); design §5.1 enumerates only Argo, Flux, Kargo, Compose; design §2.2 Environment has 'GitOps binding (tool, CR ref, path, branch…)' with no controller-less option.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `layers:` list (file, pointerPrefix, rank, owner) in `.zhi/environments/<env>.yaml` as first-class fallback discovery in M1; add Helmfile (`environments`, `releases[].values`) and Fleet (`fleet.yaml helm.valuesFiles`) as declarative file-pattern maps (the §8 'Layout discovery: fixed core + declarative file-pattern maps' row already allows this); add 'how do your customers run Helm: Argo / Flux / Helmfile / CI helm upgrade / Fleet' to S14.

findings.section: §4(a) `values.schema.json` and the `x-zhi` vocabulary; S5 pass criterion
findings.claim_or_choice: 'the `x-zhi` vocabulary is declared with `$vocabulary` and registered as a custom vocabulary … so hints are type-checked by zhi and treated as annotations by every other validator by spec, not by luck'.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Per JSON Schema 2020-12 core, '$vocabulary MUST be ignored in schema documents that are not being processed as a meta-schema' and it 'MUST NOT appear in subschemas'; a `values.schema.json` is not a meta-schema, so the line is a no-op. Unknown keywords are already 'treated as annotations' by spec without it. To actually declare a vocabulary you must point `$schema` at a custom meta-schema, which Helm 4 / jsonschema v6 would then have to resolve offline — breaking the 'Helm 4 validates it natively' property. As written, S5 could 'pass' (annotations ignored) while the mechanism it certifies does nothing.
findings.evidence: Live check: json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core §8.1.2 ('The "$vocabulary" keyword MUST be ignored in schema documents that are not being processed as a meta-schema'; 'Unknown keywords SHOULD be treated as annotations'). Design §4(a) JSON example; embed brief §4.3 as cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the `$vocabulary` entry from the shipped schema; register the `x-zhi-*` vocabulary only inside zhi's own jsonschema/v6 compiler (that is where type-checking happens anyway); keep `$schema` at the standard 2020-12 URI; add to S5: 'with `$schema` unchanged, `helm lint`/`helm template` on Helm 4.3 accept the file and Argo CD renders it'.

findings.section: §5.3 Hydrated branches and promotion hooks vs §0 item 13 'Not built: an in-cluster component' and §3.6 'Loopback, single user'
findings.claim_or_choice: 'for Kargo OSS … `zhi check` can be called from the built-in `http` step'; 'for gitops-promoter zhi is a `CommitStatus` provider'.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Kargo's `http` step makes an outbound request from the Kargo controller to a URL — 'your server must be reachable from the Kargo deployment' — and cannot run a local CLI; gitops-promoter's gates are `promoter.argoproj.io` custom resources (e.g. `kind: DependentsSuccessfulCommitStatus`) that something with cluster write access must create. Both require a hosted endpoint or an in-cluster writer, which the design explicitly does not build. The only Kargo OSS integration that actually works with zhi-as-CLI is the one the competitors brief named: zhi's PR is what `git-wait-for-pr`/`git-merge-pr` wait on.
findings.evidence: Live check: docs.kargo.io promotion-steps/http ('enables outbound requests from the Kargo controller … cannot execute local CLI commands'); live check: argoproj-labs/gitops-promoter README (CommitStatus CRD example) and docs ('CommitStatus API for promotion gating'); competitors brief 'Kargo — settled' ('zhi should produce commits/PRs that Kargo's git-open-pr/hydrated-branch flows consume').
findings.suggested_fix: Either strike the `http`-step and CommitStatus-provider lines and keep 'zhi opens the PR Kargo waits on; `zhi check` runs as the SCM check Kargo/promoter already observe', or add a phase-2 `zhi serve` (stateless HTTP wrapper over `pkg/pipeline`) plus a ~200-LOC CommitStatus writer and amend §0 item 13 to 'no in-cluster component in v1'. Do not leave the contradiction.

findings.section: §3.2 step 5, §5.4 'digest must equal trailer', §0 item 5
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi check` 'fails on a report-digest mismatch with the trailer'; 'the digest in the commit trailer must match the check run'.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Ordinary PR life breaks this: a reviewer fixup commit or Renovate rebase after `zhi propose` has no trailer or a stale one; a different pinned Kyverno CLI, cosign, or snapshot cache state on the runner vs the laptop yields a different digest. Each produces a red check unrelated to the change. That is the Monokle/Datree friction lesson relocated *inside* the push path — the fastest route to the check being dropped from branch protection.
findings.evidence: Design §3.2 step 5 and §5.4; competitors brief Task C Monokle row ('Validation must sit in the push path (PR), not in a separate editor people must adopt') — friction in the push path is worse than friction outside it; engine-first §6 / pr-native §4.2 step 5 as adopted.
findings.suggested_fix: Digest equality is evaluated only for the exact commit carrying `Zhi-Report`, reported as Info ('report reproduced') or Warning ('report differs from proposer's: <reason>'); Blocking is decided solely by the bot's own re-run. Keep byte-identical reports as an internal property tested in CI, not as a merge gate.

findings.section: §3.5 freshness / §5.4 'refuses to clear Blocking when any snapshot exceeds maxAge'; §1.5 'platform teams get a third role for free'
findings.claim_or_choice: Stale snapshot ⇒ `zhi check` refuses to clear Blocking; refresh is a scheduled job the platform team owns.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: At a customer the platform team is not the buyer and may never run the refresh job; the consultant re-imports by hand or the check fails every PR with 'snapshot stale'. A gate that fails for reasons the PR author cannot fix is the pattern that gets a check removed. 'For free' is the adoption gate, not a bonus.
findings.evidence: Design §1.5 and §5.4; report §5.3 'refuse to clear Blocking findings on snapshots older than N days'; competitors brief Task C (Kubevious/Kubeapps: tools that depend on someone else operating a component stall).
findings.suggested_fix: Default stale ⇒ evaluate anyway, add an age badge and a Warning; `maxAge: blocking` is a per-environment opt-in for prod; `zhi check` output names who last refreshed and how (`zhi snapshot refresh` one-liner) so the fix is in the PR comment.

findings.section: §0 item 3 cut order (GitLab second-to-cut); §3.1 `internal/scm/github`; §3.8 CI
findings.claim_or_choice: GitHub bot mode is the M1 wedge; GitLab is phase 2 and the second item cut under schedule pressure.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The deployer persona pushes into the customer's or tenant's repo, and the customer chooses the SCM; European enterprise/on-prem estates are heavily GitLab (and Azure DevOps/Bitbucket). If the check only exists as a GitHub Check Run, the 'validation in the push path for every PR author' argument (§0 item 2) is false at those customers, and the persona for whom the tool is built is the one cut. I could not verify the company's SCM mix — that is the point: it is not in S14.
findings.evidence: Design §0 items 2–3, §3.1, §3.8; competitors brief Task C Monokle lesson; persona definition ('deploy the software into cloud environments (customer or per-tenant)').
findings.suggested_fix: Make `zhi check` SCM-agnostic in M1: exit code + markdown/SARIF/JSON files any CI can post; the GitHub Check Run is the only GitHub-specific ~200 LOC; add SCM mix to S14 and promote GitLab MR-note posting into M1 if customers are >~30 % GitLab; move GitLab down the cut list below LSP/MCP.

findings.section: §6 Docker Compose (phase 2); §0 item 13; cut order in §0 item 3
findings.claim_or_choice: Compose is phase 2 (~month 12–13) and 5th in the cut order; 'the domain model is target-agnostic from day one so Compose lands without a migration'.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The owner named Compose in the same breath as Kubernetes and the report calls it 'a first-class second target … not an afterthought'; the design gives Compose users nothing for a year and lists it as cuttable. Meanwhile 'target-agnostic from day one' is asserted, not tested: without a Compose fixture in M1, K8s-specific assumptions (Target identity by `kube-system` UID, `namespaces/` layer, PSA/quota stages, `x-zhi-cluster-ref` enum) will harden and phase-2 Compose becomes the migration the design claims to avoid.
findings.evidence: Owner's ask ('especially in Kubernetes and in Docker Compose'); report §1 ('Compose is a first-class second target … not an afterthought') and §9 #17 [must]; design §6, §0 items 3 and 13; report §3.1 class 17.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the Compose renderer in phase 2 but add an M1 acceptance test: a `kind: compose` package that loads, folds `.env`/override layers, and produces JSON-Schema-stage findings with pointers through `pkg/pipeline` — no host snapshot yet. Remove Compose from the cut list (it is already deferred; cutting a deferral is a second cut) and tell the owner explicitly that Compose value arrives ~month 12.

findings.section: §1.2 developers 'never leave their tooling'; §4 'three standard-shaped files'
findings.claim_or_choice: `values.cel.yaml` (helm-cel pattern) and `zhi/requirements.yaml` (Troubleshoot analyzers) are 'standard-shaped' and developers stay in their tooling.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Only `values.schema.json` is enforced by anything outside zhi. helm-cel is a small MIT side project Helm never evaluates; Troubleshoot analyzers are Replicated's vocabulary run by `kubectl preflight` at Replicated customers. Developers must learn CEL and two zhi-only files; the realistic majority case is a chart with no CEL and no requirements, so the deployer's experience is defined by the synthesised overlay, not the contract.
findings.evidence: Competitors brief Task B ('helm-cel (idsulik, MIT; HN Nov 2024)'); persona brief tools table (Troubleshoot: Replicated's preflight format); report §2 ('in a minority of charts — a values.schema.json').
findings.suggested_fix: Call them 'standard-compatible', make `zhi contract init` synthesise requirements automatically from `Chart.yaml kubeVersion` + rendered kinds/APIs + referenced classes, and make the no-developer-contract path the primary MVP demo, not the fallback.

findings.section: §1.1 thesis and §11 'Two-year survival'; report §8 'what nobody does' #2
findings.claim_or_choice: Whole-chain offline evaluation (incl. PSA and Kyverno with cluster context) is unique; only Flux Schema is named as the commoditiser.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Kyverno's `validate.podSecurity` rule already runs the Kubernetes pod-security-admission library offline via `kyverno apply`, and the Kyverno Playground backend (published 2026-09-02) already exposes `LoadClusterResources`, `LoadVAPBindings`, `LoadPolicyExceptions`, `LoadCRDs` and `OpenAPIClient(cluster, …)`. A Kyverno/Nirmata 'export cluster context + playground' release inside 12 months would cover VAP + Kyverno + PSA + CRD schema for Kyverno shops. What no one else has is quota/LimitRange arithmetic, controller-RBAC, classes/inventory catalogs, the two-persona contract, and the PR writer.
findings.evidence: Live check: kyverno.io validate docs ('By integrating the same libraries as used in Kubernetes' Pod Security Admission … Testing … in a CI/CD pipeline is enabled via the Kyverno CLI'); live check: pkg.go.dev kyverno/playground/backend/pkg/playground; report §4.3 Kyverno row.
findings.suggested_fix: Sharpen the landing-page differentiation to the five items above; keep the Kyverno-context export adapter (§3.5) in M1 so Kyverno-native platform teams can adopt the snapshot without adopting the engine — that is the 'interop hub' hedge §11 already wants.

findings.section: §11 'Two-year survival' and §3.8 distribution
findings.claim_or_choice: Flux Schema will commoditise the CRD/CEL layer; survival is the snapshot as interop hub with export adapters.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Correct but incomplete: Flux Schema ships weekly (v0.13.0 2026-09-09), ControlPlane sells Operator + Web UI (AGPL) with a public MCP, and community guides already validate `HelmRelease.spec.values` against chart schemas with composite schemas — i.e. the contract stage for Flux estates is being absorbed. The design lists no cheap distribution channel into that ecosystem.
findings.evidence: Competitors brief Flux Schema section and Flux CLI plugin row (three plugins today, third-party PR to catalog); report §4.1; WebSearch results 2026-03..07 on HelmRelease values validation.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship zhi as a `flux-zhi` CLI plugin (RFC-0013 catalog PR, SHA-256 + digest pin) and a krew plugin from M1; confirm the flux-schema/kubeconform/Kyverno export adapters are M1 deliverables, not phase 2.

findings.section: §3.5 developer-safe slice
findings.claim_or_choice: The `developer-safe` slice (discovery, OpenAPI, CRDs, admission policies + params, engine policies, catalogs) can cross the invisible border to vendor developers.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: VAP/Kyverno/Gatekeeper policy bodies and params (allowed registries, internal hostnames, exempted namespaces), SCC lists and catalog names are customer-confidential at regulated customers; 'developer-safe' is zhi's judgement, not the customer's approval, and the slice will leak the customer's security posture to a third party.
findings.evidence: Design §3.5 slice annotations; ecosystem lens advice 3 as cited in §0 item 7; persona definition (consultants deploy into customer environments).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `contract-only` slice (discovery + OpenAPI + CRDs) as the default border-crossing artifact; make slices customer-selectable with a redaction-policy digest recorded in `manifest.json`; document that policy bodies never leave without explicit customer opt-in.

findings.section: §5.4 'Renovate, Kargo and human PRs are validated uniformly'; §5.6 'adapters run with no network'; §0 item 9 `--strict`
findings.claim_or_choice: Bot mode has no network and `--strict` promotes unobserved inputs to Warnings by default.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Renovate/Image-Updater PRs touch only machine-managed image tags; the only meaningful check (tag existence via registry HEAD) is unobservable offline, so every such PR gets an 'unobserved' Warning under `--strict` — recurring noise on the highest-volume PR class, which trains people to ignore the check.
findings.evidence: Design §5.4, §5.6, §6 ('image tag existence via registry HEAD when online'); report §3.1 class 11 ('tag existence needs registry HEAD when online').
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt changes confined to machine-owned pointers from unobserved promotion, or allow-list registry HEAD in bot mode under `allowEgress: [registry]`; report 'no new findings vs base' as the headline for pure machine PRs.

findings.section: §0 item 14 MVP definition vs §11 'we do not compete on form UI' vs §13 post-mortems
findings.claim_or_choice: The MVP is defined 'with a form' and the form is 'the last thing cut', while survival explicitly disclaims competing on form UI.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Form-first Kubernetes UIs are the category with the worst survival record in the evidence (Cyclops slowing, Kubeapps archived, Glasskube archived, Weave GitOps dead); leading with the form in positioning invites comparison with Devtron and Cyclops on their strongest axis and hides the actual moat.
findings.evidence: Competitors brief Task C (Cyclops, Glasskube, Kubeapps, Weave GitOps rows); design §0 item 14, §11 last bullet.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the form in the MVP for the consultant, but make §0 item 1's sentence ('the PR check that already knows your cluster') the only positioning line; the form is described as 'the consultant's editor for that check', never as the product.

what_is_right: Positioning as a check/PR provider beside Argo, Flux, Kargo and gitops-promoter rather than a UI for them or a new source of truth — the exact inverse of the Weave GitOps, Kubevious, Kubeapps, Cyclops and ConfigHub shapes (competitors brief Task C; report §8 last paragraph). Do not let a reviser drift toward an in-cluster component or a hosted control plane.

Git as the only write target with DRY-repo PRs primary and `allowDirectPush` off by default; provenance as commit trailers in Argo's own `hydrator.metadata` shape (report §9 #1; §10.1 DRY-centric verdict).
Bot in the push path before any editor (`zhi validate --exit-code` → `zhi check`) as M1 — the ordering the Monokle and Datree post-mortems demand (competitors brief Task C).
The deployer-owned contract overlay at `.zhi/contracts/<package>/` for charts the consultant cannot push to (Bitnami/vendor charts); this is the single most persona-correct decision in the design.

No chart migration: consume `values.schema.json`, `# @schema`, ytt, Timoni, XRD/CRD, Rancher `questions.yaml`, OLM descriptors; synthesise when absent; emit standard `values.schema.json` so Helm 4 enforces it for free (report §6.1–6.2; Glasskube lesson 'do not fight Helm').

Embed k8s.io v0.37.0 staging modules with no replaces, vendor-fork the three in-tree packages, shell out to the Kyverno CLI with zhi-owned exit codes, keep OPA/Gatekeeper out of go.mod until Rego is needed (report §10.1 'Shell out to the CLI' verdict; embed brief).
Fidelity in the Finding type with `unobserved[]` and never 'will apply' copy; T2 live dry-run as calibration oracle (Kyverno #5476 'passes with kyverno apply, fails in cluster'; report §5.3).

Shallow plugin system: zero loadable plugins in v1, two Go-interface doors, exec `checks:` digest-pinned in a lockfile, no marketplace until a second implementor exists — matches all 17 briefs and Kubernetes/Flux/Kyverno/Renovate practice (report §7.3; audit lesson 6).

CEL as the only rule language via `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/environment`; Yaegi dropped; server-side visibility map so the browser runs no second expression language (Rancher #4706 Ember/Jexl lesson).
OpenShift in the MVP as a data-tier profile with SCC emulation gated on a spike — the only distribution decision that matches a consultancy's real customers (deployer brief; persona lens advice 1).

Export adapters to kubeconform, kubectl-validate, Kyverno context, gator and flux-schema layouts, plus SARIF/PolicyReport output — this is the interop hedge that keeps the snapshot valuable if the evaluation half commoditises (report §9 #22).
Bot-mode security rules: digest-pinned exec binaries, no network, scratch HOME, `allowExec` owned by the deployer side via CODEOWNERS (ecosystem lens fatal flaw 2 as adopted in §5.6).

Kargo OSS integration via the PR that `git-wait-for-pr`/`git-merge-pr` wait on (the one Kargo path that is actually OSS — competitors brief 'Kargo — settled'); keep this line when fixing the `http`-step contradiction.
Fifteen spikes with pass/fail criteria before architecture freeze, including S14 practitioner survey; the honest refusal to promise '<2 s' or Helm source maps.

lens: Skeptical Kubernetes API-machinery engineer (offline admission fidelity, embedding feasibility, snapshot completeness, PR/Git mechanics, estimates)
verdict: The dependency decisions are sound and verifiable (k8s.io v0.37 without replaces, Kyverno by subprocess, kubectl-validate's strategy path for CRD CEL, Helm v4 SDK with ClientProvider-backed lookup), so the design is buildable. What is wrong is inside the thing the product is for: the §3.3 chain does not mirror the apiserver (PodSecurity, ResourceQuota, LimitRanger-validate and CRD CEL run before MAP/Kyverno mutation, whereas the real chain runs every mutator first, then BeforeCreate, then every validator with ResourceQuota last), workload expansion ignores that the expanded Pods are created by kube-system controllers and that Kyverno autogen already covers controllers (double counting, wrong userInfo), and the quota arithmetic ignores rollout surge, scopes and the old revision's pods. Two spikes have premises that are already known to be false: S4 is a port, not a vendor-fork, because LimitRanger and the quota evaluators take internal `pkg/apis/core` types; S11 cannot "build with no replaces" because `sccmatching` imports `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core` and apiserver-library-go requires the `k8s.io/kubernetes` module. The `$vocabulary` mechanism in §4(a) is a spec no-op, the pure-function/digest-match promise breaks on every chart that calls `randAlphaNum` and on every human fix-up commit, and the OpenShift project-template injection predicts constraints that a GitOps-created `kind: Namespace` never receives. The LOC-based calendar argues from the wrong constraint: this repo's own history shows ~21k non-test LOC/month from one person, ten times the design's assumed rate, so the schedule should be justified by calibration work, not LOC. None of this is fatal; every item is a section-level correction.

findings.section: §3.3 Render → validate pipeline (stages 5–11) and §0 item 8
findings.claim_or_choice: "The order mirrors the apiserver so mutation precedes validation": stages run as structural/CRD-CEL (5) → NamespaceLifecycle (6) → LimitRanger mutate+validate (7) → PodSecurity (8) → ResourceQuota (9) → MAP + Kyverno mutate (10) → VAP/Kyverno validate (11).
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The real apiserver runs ALL mutating plugins' Admit in plugin order (LimitRanger, ServiceAccount, Priority, DefaultTolerationSeconds, DefaultStorageClass, RuntimeClass, DefaultIngressClass, …, MutatingAdmissionPolicy, MutatingAdmissionWebhook), then rest.BeforeCreate (defaulting + strategy.Validate incl. CRD CEL), then ALL validating plugins' Validate in order (NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger, PodSecurity, …, ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, ValidatingAdmissionWebhook, ResourceQuota last). PodSecurity and ResourceQuota are validation-only plugins. In the design, a MAP or Kyverno mutate rule that injects securityContext or default resources (the two most common mutations) is evaluated AFTER PSA and quota have already produced their verdicts, so PSA/quota/CRD-CEL results are wrong on exactly the clusters that have mutation policies (and on OpenShift, where SCC mutation precedes PSA). ServiceAccount/Priority/DefaultStorageClass mutators are absent although they feed quota scopes (PriorityClass-scoped quota, `<sc>.storageclass.storage.k8s.io/requests.storage`) and reference checks.
findings.evidence: kubernetes release-1.37 `pkg/kubeapiserver/options/plugins.go` AllOrderedPlugins ("webhook, resourcequota, and deny plugins must go at the end"); `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/chain.go` Admit iterates MutationInterface, Validate iterates ValidationInterface; `registry/generic/registry/store.go` Create: `rest.BeforeCreate` then `createValidation` ("at this point we have a fully formed object. It is time to call the validators"); `plugin/pkg/admission/security/podsecurity/admission.go` `var _ admission.ValidationInterface = &Plugin{}` (no Admit); `apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/resourcequota/admission.go` `var _ admission.ValidationInterface = &QuotaAdmission{}`; policy brief pain-point "Mutation precedes validation but tools validate pre-mutation objects".
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite stages as three phases: (M) mutators in apiserver order — LimitRanger defaults, ServiceAccount (default SA, imagePullSecrets), Priority (resolve priorityClassName), DefaultStorageClass, RuntimeClass, DefaultIngressClass, MAP, Kyverno mutate (first CLI pass, take patched output), profile mutators (SCC assign); (S) decode-level defaulting/pruning + structural schema + CRD CEL on the mutated object; (V) validators in order — NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger validate, PodSecurity, Priority/RuntimeClass existence, VAP, Kyverno validate (second CLI pass on mutated objects) + generated-VAP Gatekeeper, webhook match, ResourceQuota last. Show the M-phase diff as "what the cluster will store". Keep discovery, expansion, RBAC, references, immutables and requirements as zhi-specific pre/post stages but stop calling the current order apiserver-mirroring.

findings.section: §3.3 stage 4 (Expand) with stages 8, 11, 13
findings.claim_or_choice: Expand workloads to Pod templates (gator-expand / Kyverno-autogen style) and run the same chain with the controller identity (Argo/Flux SA) via `--userinfo` and the RBAC authorizer.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: (1) The Pods produced by a Deployment are created by `system:serviceaccount:kube-system:replicaset-controller` (Job/CronJob/StatefulSet/DaemonSet controllers likewise), not by the GitOps SA; VAP `request.userInfo`, `authorizer`, Kyverno `--userinfo`, and matchConditions that exclude system service accounts evaluate against the wrong identity for every expanded object. (2) PSA enforce applies only to the resulting Pods, never to workload templates — the expansion is correct for PSA but only if the expanded Pod carries template labels, `pod-template-hash` and ownerReferences that label/owner-selecting policies see. (3) Kyverno already evaluates Pod rules on controllers through autogen; feeding both the Deployment and its expanded Pods to `kyverno apply` double-reports every violation and produces two findings with different resource identities for one values pointer.
findings.evidence: kubernetes.io Pod Security Admission: "enforce mode is not applied to workload resources, only to the resulting pod objects"; Kyverno autogen docs: rules auto-generated for DaemonSet, Deployment, Job, StatefulSet, ReplicaSet, ReplicationController, CronJob, translating `spec.containers` to `spec.template.spec.containers`; plugins.go AllOrderedPlugins shows PodSecurity as a per-request plugin evaluated with the request's userInfo; policy brief design implication 6 (model admission context explicitly: identity, operation, oldObject).
findings.suggested_fix: Give every expanded object its own admission context: user = the owning controller's SA, operation CREATE, ownerReferences and pod-template-hash synthesised, namespace inherited. Route objects per engine: engines with autogen (Kyverno) receive unexpanded workloads only; native stages (PSA, quota, LimitRanger, VAP, generated-VAP) receive expanded Pods; dedupe findings by (engine, ruleId, template pointer). Record the identity used in `Finding.fidelity.unobserved` when the snapshot lacks the controller SA's RBAC.

findings.section: §3.3 stage 9 (ResourceQuota) and §3.5 inventory layer
findings.claim_or_choice: Quota is `(used + delta) ≤ hard` per namespace across all documents in the change, with `status.used` staleness as a Warning.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: That arithmetic is the steady-state check only. Quota is charged per Pod at creation: (a) a rolling update with default `maxSurge: 25%` creates new pods while old ones still count, so a Deployment already at the limit fails to roll even though its final state fits; (b) `delta` must subtract the previous revision's pods of the same workload (already in `used`) and multiply by replicas — the inventory layer stores "workloads (oldObject)" but no Pods or per-workload usage; (c) scopes/`scopeSelector` (PriorityClass, BestEffort, Terminating, CrossNamespacePodAffinity) and `count/<resource>.<group>` object counts are not mentioned; (d) storage-class-scoped PVC quota needs DefaultStorageClass mutation to have run first (see order finding). The design's OpenShift ClusterResourceQuota summation inherits all of these.
findings.evidence: cluster-state-import brief pain-point: "Creating a Deployment that exceeds quota succeeds, but Pods within it will fail"; release-1.37 `pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/pods.go` (usage is per Pod, uses `MatchingScopes` and `resourcehelper.PodRequests`); kubernetes Deployment docs `maxSurge` default 25%; §3.5 inventory lists workloads (oldObject) but not Pods.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute two numbers per namespace and report both: steady state (used − oldPods(workload) + replicas × podUsage) and rollout peak (steady + surge pods, honouring maxSurge/maxUnavailable, StatefulSet/DaemonSet semantics, Job parallelism). Carry quota scopes via the ported `MatchingScopes`. Add per-namespace Pod requests (aggregated, no secrets) to the `full` slice so the old-revision subtraction is computable; otherwise label the quota finding `approximate`.

findings.section: §3.1 `third_party/k8s`, §10.1 S4, §10.2 size table ("~2k forks")
findings.claim_or_choice: Vendor-fork `limitranger`, `rbac.RulesAllow` and `evaluator/core` from kubernetes@v1.37.0 as "pure functions over API types" (~2k LOC), pass criterion "builds with no replaces".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: They are not functions over external API types. `PodValidateLimitFunc(limitRange *corev1.LimitRange, pod *api.Pod)` and `PodMutateLimitFunc` take the INTERNAL `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core.Pod`; `evaluator/core/pods.go` imports `pkg/apis/core`, `pkg/apis/core/v1` (generated conversion), `pkg/apis/core/v1/helper`, `helper/qos`, `pkg/features`, `pkg/scheduler/util`; `rbac.go` imports `pkg/apis/rbac/v1` and `pkg/registry/rbac/validation`. Copying them means dragging the internal type tree and its ~10k-line conversion; the real work is a port to `corev1` types that must be re-done every minor. The embed brief itself flagged this as UNVERIFIED; the design promoted it to a size estimate.
findings.evidence: pkg.go.dev k8s.io/kubernetes@v1.37.0/plugin/pkg/admission/limitranger signatures (pod `*api.Pod` = `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core`); release-1.37 `pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/pods.go` import block; release-1.37 `plugin/pkg/auth/authorizer/rbac/rbac.go` import block; embed brief §5 ("UNVERIFIED for evaluator/core helpers — check pkg/apis/core imports").
findings.suggested_fix: Rename S4 to "port" with its own pass criterion: LimitRanger mutate/validate and pod/PVC/service quota usage re-typed to `k8s.io/api/core/v1` using `k8s.io/component-helpers/resource.PodRequests` and `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/quota/v1/generic`, with a golden test against `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` on kind; keep `RulesAllow`/`RuleAllows` (external types) and write a ~150-line rule resolver over the snapshot's Roles/Bindings instead of importing `pkg/registry/rbac/validation`. Budget a per-minor refresh task and drop the "~2k LOC copy" figure.

findings.section: §0 item 10, §7 (SCC emulation), §10.1 S11
findings.claim_or_choice: S11: "`openshift/apiserver-library-go` `sccmatching` builds against k8s.io v0.37.0 with no replaces"; SCC emulation gated on this spike.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The premise is already refutable without running the spike. `sccmatching/matcher.go` imports `kapi "k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core"` and `k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/apis/core/pods` (internal types; `AssignSecurityContext(provider, pod *kapi.Pod, …)`), and apiserver-library-go's go.mod requires `k8s.io/kubernetes v1.36.2` plus k8s.io/* v0.36.2 and openshift/{api,client-go,library-go}. Importing it forces the `k8s.io/kubernetes` module into zhi's build, whose published go.mod needs the ~33 staging replaces the embed brief says to avoid, and pins the OpenShift fork's version train, not v0.37.0. "No replaces" and "v0.37.0" cannot both hold.
findings.evidence: raw apiserver-library-go go.mod (`k8s.io/kubernetes v1.36.2`, k8s.io/* v0.36.2); raw `pkg/securitycontextconstraints/sccmatching/matcher.go` import block; embed brief §0.1 and [36] (k8s.io/kubernetes published .mod requires `k8s.io/api v0.0.0` with 33 replaces).
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe S11 as a port-sizing spike: count LOC of `sccmatching` + `util/sort` + the provider strategies (uid/gid/selinux/seccomp/capabilities/fsgroup) and the `library-go/pkg/security/uid` range parser, and decide port-vs-data-tier on that number and on the `oc adm policy scc-subject-review` calibration. Decision 10 should say "SCC emulation is a port of OpenShift code to external types, gated on S11", not "builds without replaces".

findings.section: §4 (a) `values.schema.json` and §10.1 S5
findings.claim_or_choice: Declare the `x-zhi` vocabulary with `$vocabulary: {"https://zhi.dev/vocab/ui/v1": false}` inside values.schema.json and register it in jsonschema/v6 "so hints are type-checked by zhi and treated as annotations by every other validator by spec, not by luck".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: JSON Schema 2020-12 says `$vocabulary` "MUST be ignored in schema documents that are not being processed as a meta-schema"; a values.schema.json whose `$schema` is the standard 2020-12 meta-schema is never processed as a meta-schema, so the line is a no-op for zhi, Helm and everyone else. Unknown `x-zhi-*` keywords are treated as annotations by spec regardless (§6.5), so the "by spec" property comes from the unknown-keyword rule, not from `$vocabulary`. In jsonschema/v6, vocabularies for 2020-12 are "disabled unless metaschema enables a vocabulary" and the way to type-check custom keywords without a custom meta-schema is `Compiler.RegisterVocabulary` + `Compiler.AssertVocabs()`. The tempting alternative — a custom `$schema` meta-schema — would make Helm 4's `SchemeURLLoader` fetch it over https (15 s timeout) on every `helm install`, exactly the failure the design wants to avoid.
findings.evidence: json-schema.org draft 2020-12 core (`$vocabulary` "MUST be ignored in schema documents that are not being processed as a meta-schema"; unrecognized keywords treated as annotations); pkg.go.dev santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema/v6 v6.0.3: `RegisterVocabulary`, `AssertVocabs` ("for draft/2020-12: disabled unless metaschema enables a vocabulary"); embed brief §4.3 (Helm 4 https loader, 15 s timeout).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove `$vocabulary` from the example and text. State: schemas keep the standard `$schema`; zhi's compiler calls `RegisterVocabulary(zhiVocab)` then `AssertVocabs()` so `x-zhi-*` are syntax-checked by zhi; other validators ignore them as annotations per §6.5. Make S5's pass criterion "helm install/template with a schema carrying x-zhi-* keywords produces no warning and no network access".

findings.section: §0 item 5, §3.2 step 5, §5.2 trailers, §5.4 (`zhi check` digest match)
findings.claim_or_choice: `pkg/pipeline.Validate` is a pure function of committed inputs plus snapshot digest; `zhi check` fails with "report mismatch" unless its report digest equals the `Zhi-Report` trailer; `Zhi-Rendered` is a trailer.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: (1) Helm rendering is not pure: Sprig `randAlphaNum`/`randAlpha`/`uuidv4`/`now`/`genCA`/`genSelfSignedCert`/`derivePassword`/`htpasswd`/`bcrypt` are common (Bitnami `common.secrets.passwords.manage` generates a password whenever `lookup` finds none — and with a names-only inventory it always finds none), so the rendered set, its digest and any finding that quotes a rendered value differ per run; the digest-match rule then fails legitimately proposed PRs. (2) The rule as written also fails every PR whose head commit is not zhi's — human fix-up commits, GitHub "Update branch" merges, Renovate/Kargo PRs (no trailer) — and every PR whose `zhi.lock` snapshot digest moved on main after the proposal (a legitimately different report, not a mismatch).
findings.evidence: pkg.go.dev helm.sh/helm/v4@v4.3.0/pkg/engine: `Engine.CustomTemplateFuncs template.FuncMap` (override point exists) and `RenderWithClientProvider`; inner-loop brief Source Hydrator constraints ("No deterministic external lookups"); §5.4 says Renovate/Kargo/human PRs are validated uniformly, which the mismatch rule contradicts.
findings.suggested_fix: (a) Install deterministic replacements for the non-deterministic Sprig functions via `CustomTemplateFuncs` (seeded from the report inputs or a fixed sentinel) and tag Secrets that contain such values as `generated-at-render` so their content is excluded from diffs and digests; render twice in the golden suite to detect residual nondeterminism. (b) Enforce digest equality only when the head commit carries `Zhi-Report` AND its `Zhi-Snapshot`/`Zhi-Profile` digests equal the lockfile's; otherwise compute fresh and mark the PR "proposal stale, re-validated". Drop `Zhi-Rendered` from the must-match set.

findings.section: §3.5 snapshot layers (`inventory/` "names+keys only: Secrets, ConfigMaps"; `gitops/ substituteFrom (keyed, redacted)`; `rbac/ subjectrules/<identity>`), §1.3 and §3.5 RBAC generator
findings.claim_or_choice: Redact ConfigMaps to names+keys; capture `SelfSubjectRulesReview` for the controller identity; `zhi snapshot rbac` emits a minimal read-only ClusterRole a bank's security team will accept.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: (1) ConfigMap DATA is an input to three stages the design relies on: Kyverno `context.configMap` (`{{ name.data.key }}` allow-lists, registries), Flux `postBuild.substituteFrom` ConfigMaps (the values are what gets substituted; without them every `${VAR}` without default becomes a false Blocking under the design's own kustomize-controller strictness rule), and Helm `lookup` on ConfigMaps. Redacting them silently breaks stages 2, 11 and §5.1 Flux discovery. (2) `SelfSubjectRulesReview` is by definition the caller's own rules; capturing the Argo/Flux SA's rules requires the `impersonate` verb, which is precisely what a security review rejects — while the `rbac/` layer already holds the Roles/Bindings needed to resolve it offline. (3) "Names+keys only" for Secrets still requires `list secrets` cluster-wide, and the API returns full data over the wire (PartialObjectMetadata returns metadata without `data` keys); the generated ClusterRole is therefore not "minimal" in the sense a bank reads it, and the design does not say the layer is optional/degradable.
findings.evidence: Kyverno external-data-sources docs (`context.configMap` → `{{ <context-name>.data.<key-name> }}`); design §5.1 (substituteFrom, missing variable without default = Blocking); cluster-state-import brief (RBAC snapshot-able via `kubectl auth can-i --list --as=...`, i.e. impersonation); kubernetes API concepts: PartialObjectMetadata alternate representation returns metadata only.
findings.suggested_fix: Split `inventory/`: ConfigMaps verbatim in the `full` slice with an operator deny-list (names/namespaces/keys), Secrets as names+keys with optional length-preserving sentinels; document that the Secrets layer needs `list secrets` and make it a degradable layer the RBAC generator prints in red. Resolve controller RBAC offline from `rbac/` (Roles, Bindings, ClusterRoles) using a local rule resolver; drop `subjectrules/` from the importer's default path and offer it only when the importer runs as that identity.

findings.section: §3.3 stage 6 and §7 OpenShift data tier ("project-request template injection")
findings.claim_or_choice: For namespaces the PR creates on OpenShift, inject the project-request template's quota/LimitRange/NetworkPolicy into the pseudo cluster before evaluation.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The template is applied by the `projectrequests.project.openshift.io` REST path (openshift-apiserver loads `projectRequestTemplate`, processes it and creates the Project plus the template's RoleBindings/quotas/etc.). A `kind: Namespace` created by Argo (`CreateNamespace=true`) or committed in a Flux Kustomization never goes through that path, so those namespaces receive none of the template's objects. Injecting them predicts quota/LimitRange denials that will not happen and, worse, hides the real outcome: the GitOps-created namespace has no NetworkPolicy, no RoleBindings and no quota until someone adds them.
findings.evidence: openshift/openshift-apiserver `pkg/project/apiserver/registry/projectrequest/delegated/delegated.go` Create: `getTemplate` → `ProcessToList` → create Project → create remaining template objects; "This is the REST handler for ProjectRequest resources". Argo CD sync option `CreateNamespace=true` creates a Namespace object (design §5.1 discovery already parses Applications).
findings.suggested_fix: Make template injection conditional on a per-environment declaration (`namespaceProvisioning: projectrequest | direct`) in `.zhi/environments/<env>.yaml`/`declared.yaml`; default `direct` for Argo/Flux estates. In `direct` mode emit an Info/Warning finding "namespace created directly by the controller; project template (quota/LimitRange/NetworkPolicy/RoleBindings) will not be applied" and evaluate against no template.

findings.section: §0 item 14, §10.2 ("≈26–30k non-test Go LOC, eight months for two people, twelve-plus for one", size table)
findings.claim_or_choice: The calendar is argued from LOC: M1 ≈ 15k LOC in months 2–4, MVP ≈ 26–30k LOC in 8 months for two people; tests near 1:1 "as today".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: LOC is demonstrably not this owner's constraint. This repository's history shows +10.5k (Jan 2026) and +31.9k (Feb 2026) non-test, non-generated Go lines plus +40.6k test lines, from one person (two Git identities), i.e. ~21k non-test LOC/month during the build burst — roughly ten times the ~1.7k LOC/person-month the design assumes. Arguing the schedule from LOC therefore both overstates the writing effort and understates the actual bottleneck: calibrating an admission emulator against real clusters (fixture clusters, T2 agreement, per-minor ports of the forked packages, profile maintenance) — the audit's own lesson being that the fast-written 42k LOC hosted zero third-party plugins.
findings.evidence: `git log --numstat` on /home/luk/Desktop/git/zhi: 2026-01 +10530/−287 non-test Go, 2026-02 +31882/−3406; tests 2026-01 +10805, 2026-02 +29761; authors MrWong99 94, Lukas Schmidt 63, dependabot 42; current tree 42,487 non-test/non-pb Go LOC, 42,290 test LOC, 10,790 pb.go (design §8 cites the same 10,790).
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the eight-month calendar if the owner wants it, but replace LOC milestones with calibration exit criteria: M1 exits when T0 agrees with `kubectl --dry-run=server` on N fixture clusters (kind + one OpenShift + one managed) for ≥X% of findings across report §3.1 classes, the golden suite renders deterministically, and the per-minor port refresh has been done once (1.36→1.37). Report LOC as an outcome, not a plan.

findings.section: §3.1 ("CEL only through k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/environment"), §4 (b), §11 version skew
findings.claim_or_choice: Import CEL only via the k8s environment package; compile `values.cel.yaml` in the k8s environment pinned to the snapshot's minor.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Binding `values`, `oldValues`, `env`, `rendered`, `snapshot` and evaluating programs requires `EnvSet.Extend(VersionedOptions{EnvOptions: []cel.EnvOption{cel.Variable(...)}})` and `cel.Program`, i.e. importing `github.com/google/cel-go/cel` directly at the path k8s pins. The literal rule cannot be followed; the real rule (embed brief) is "never import `cel.dev/cel-go`; import cel-go only at the k8s-pinned path". Also unspecified: imported cluster policies must compile with `StoredExpressions` (what the apiserver does for persisted VAP/CRD rules) while `values.cel.yaml` rules meant for promotion to VAP should compile with `NewExpressions` (write-path strictness).
findings.evidence: pkg.go.dev k8s.io/apiserver@v0.37.0/pkg/cel/environment: `MustBaseEnvSet(ver *version.Version) *EnvSet`, `Extend(options ...VersionedOptions)`, `NewExpressions` ("validate new or modified expressions in requests that write expressions"), `StoredExpressions` ("CEL expressions that have been persisted to storage"); embed brief §0.2, §2.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to "cel-go imported only at the path k8s.io/apiserver pins (currently github.com/google/cel-go v0.29.2); never cel.dev/cel-go". Specify `StoredExpressions` for snapshot policies and `NewExpressions` for contract rules; keep `MustBaseEnvSet(snapshotMinor)`.

findings.section: §3.3 stage 10 (MAP via `policy/mutating`), §10.1 S2
findings.claim_or_choice: MAP offline "via k8s.io/apiserver/.../policy/mutating" the way Gatekeeper's k8scel driver uses `validating`.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: There is no exported compile entry point for MAP: `compilePolicy(policy *v1.MutatingAdmissionPolicy) PolicyEvaluator` is unexported (compilation.go ≈ 85 lines); `NewDispatcher(authorizer.UnconditionalAuthorizer, *matching.Matcher, patch.TypeConverterManager)` is exported but `matching.NewMatcher(namespaceLister, kubernetes.Interface)` wants a lister and client, and `patch.NewTypeConverterManager(static, openapi.Client)` needs an OpenAPI client. Feasible, but it is a small fork plus fakes, not a library call.
findings.evidence: pkg.go.dev k8s.io/apiserver@v0.37.0/pkg/admission/plugin/policy/mutating (exports: NewPlugin, NewDispatcher, PolicyEvaluator{Matcher, Mutators, CompositedCompiler}, no exported compile); raw release-1.37 mutating/compilation.go (`compilePolicy`, `convertV1Variables` unexported); mutating/patch exports `NewTypeConverterManager(staticTypeConverter, openapiClient)`, `NewApplyConfigurationPatcher`, `NewJSONPatcher`; matching `NewMatcher(namespaceLister, client)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to S2: copy compilation.go into `third_party/k8s/mapcompile`, back `TypeConverterManager` with the snapshot's `openapi.Client` (the same one kubectl-validate uses), and supply a snapshot-backed NamespaceLister with a no-op client; list it in the S4 port inventory.

findings.section: §3.1 (kubectl-validate by pseudo-version), §10.1 S1
findings.claim_or_choice: kubectl-validate pinned at a pseudo-version alongside k8s.io/* v0.37.0.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: kubectl-validate main pins k8s.io/* v0.35.0 (go 1.25, no replaces); MVS will lift it to v0.37.0. `customresource.NewStrategy` has the same nine-parameter signature at release-1.35 and release-1.37, so the bump is likely fine, but nobody upstream builds that combination; S1 should verify the build, not only the verdicts.
findings.evidence: raw kubectl-validate go.mod (k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver, apimachinery, apiserver, client-go v0.35.0); raw release-1.35 and release-1.37 strategy.go `NewStrategy(typer, namespaceScoped, kind, schemaValidator, statusSchemaValidator, structuralSchema, status, scale, selectableFields)`; release-1.37 strategy.go `cel.NewValidator(structuralSchema, true, celconfig.PerCallLimit)` and `celValidator.Validate(..., celconfig.RuntimeCELCostBudget)`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "kubectl-validate main compiles and passes its own tests against k8s.io v0.37.0 under MVS" to S1's pass criterion; keep a fork-readiness note since releases lag (last tag v0.0.4).

findings.section: §5.6 bot-mode security, §3.1 `internal/git`, §3.4 T2
findings.claim_or_choice: "Every exec binary — Kyverno CLI, kwctl, cosign, git, … — is digest-pinned in zhi.lock"; "no PATH auto-detection of anything"; adapters "run with no network".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: System `git` (and `kubectl` for T2, if exec'd) changes digest with every distro update; a digest pin makes zhi refuse to run after `apt upgrade`. "No network" for a child process is not enforceable portably: Linux needs user/network namespaces (often disabled on hardened runners), macOS has nothing; it can only be engine flags (`kyverno apply` without `--cluster`, `--registry=false`) plus best-effort isolation.
findings.evidence: Design §5.6 text; audit §4.3 (apply.go subprocess runner carried for git); design §3.4 T2 mechanism; inner-loop brief (Kyverno CLI offline flags).
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt `git` from digest pinning (configured path, version floor) or use pure-Go go-git for branch/commit/push; run T2 in-process via client-go SSA dry-run (`ApplyOptions{DryRun: ["All"], FieldValidation: "Strict"}`) instead of exec'ing kubectl; reword "no network" to "engine network features disabled by flag; OS-level isolation best-effort on Linux".

findings.section: §3.5 (cosign verify by exec), §7, §9 ("unwired Sigstore stack — drop")
findings.claim_or_choice: Verify snapshot signatures by exec'ing a digest-pinned cosign v3 with `--offline --trusted-root`.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: go.mod already carries `github.com/sigstore/sigstore-go v1.3.0` (pure Go); in-process bundle verification against a pinned trusted root gives the same offline property without a ~100 MB cosign download and without the bootstrap question of who verifies cosign itself. The exec choice is defensible as audit hygiene but the design presents it as the only way to keep the chokepoint honest.
findings.evidence: /home/luk/Desktop/git/zhi/go.mod lines 19–21 (sigstore/protobuf-specs v0.5.2, sigstore v1.10.9, sigstore-go v1.3.0); audit lesson 7 as cited by the design.
findings.suggested_fix: State the alternative explicitly and pick on evidence: either sigstore-go in-process (single binary, no bootstrap) or exec cosign (operator-familiar CLI); either way the chokepoint is one function in `internal/snapshot`.

findings.section: §5.2 / §5.4 GitHub Check Run + SARIF
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi check` posts a GitHub Check Run + SARIF; branch protection can require it; PRs from forks are expected.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: SARIF upload to code scanning on private/internal repositories requires GitHub Code Security to be enabled (paid) — a consultancy's GitOps repos are private — and needs `security-events: write`, which the default token on fork PRs does not have. The Check Run with annotations (GitHub App or `checks: write`) is the reliable path; SARIF is optional output.
findings.evidence: docs.github.com "Uploading a SARIF file to GitHub": "For private and internal repositories, code scanning is available when GitHub Code Security features are enabled"; required permission `security-events: write`.
findings.suggested_fix: Make Check Run annotations the primary PR surface (batched, ≤50 per update), keep SARIF as a `--format` for shops that have Code Security; document the fork-PR token limitation and recommend a GitHub App installation for `zhi check`.

findings.section: §6 Docker Compose path
findings.claim_or_choice: Load the project "first with interpolation off to run `template.ExtractVariables`, then with the UI's mapping".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: With interpolation off, uninterpolated `${VAR}` strings sit in typed fields (`replicas`, `ports`), so the first pass must also skip schema validation and consistency checks or it fails before `ExtractVariables` runs.
findings.evidence: pkg.go.dev compose-go/v2@v2.15.0/loader Options: `SkipValidation`, `SkipInterpolation`, `SkipNormalization`, `SkipConsistencyCheck`, `SkipResolveEnvironment`; `LoadModelWithContext` returns the raw dictionary.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the first pass as `LoadModelWithContext` with `SkipInterpolation`, `SkipValidation`, `SkipConsistencyCheck`, `SkipResolveEnvironment` set; the second pass as `LoadWithContext` with the mapping and full validation.

findings.section: §3.4 fidelity tiers (T2 as calibration oracle), §10.2 months 5–6
findings.claim_or_choice: T2 (`kubectl apply --dry-run=server --validate=strict` with the controller's fieldManager) doubles as the golden-suite oracle; the T0/T2 delta is a tracked metric.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Server dry-run cannot exercise objects in a namespace the same PR creates (dry-run persists nothing, so the second object fails NamespaceLifecycle), runs as the caller's identity unless the CI credential may impersonate the controller SA (userInfo-dependent VAP/Kyverno results differ), skips side-effect webhooks, and never sees controller-created Pods — i.e. it is blind to exactly the PSA/quota classes the expansion stage exists for. Without carving these out, the delta metric carries permanent noise.
findings.evidence: fidelity brief §5 (SSD blind to new resources, mutations excluded), cluster-state-import brief (dry-run "cannot see controllers (a Deployment passes while its Pods are rejected)"), design §3.3 stage 4.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the oracle's coverage explicitly: compare only findings with `wouldFailAt: admission` on pre-existing namespaces, identity-normalised; treat expansion-derived findings as oracle-less and calibrate them against a real apply in the kind fixture instead.

findings.section: §3.3 stage 3 (Discovery "replaces pluto/kubent")
findings.claim_or_choice: Removed/deprecated GVK detection from the snapshot's discovery document replaces pluto/kubent.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Discovery shows served and preferred versions; it does not say "deprecated in 1.xx, removed in 1.yy" for versions still served, which is the Info-level signal pluto's versions.yaml provides and the design's own severity table promises ("deprecation-in → Info").
findings.evidence: cluster-state-import brief pluto row ("COPY versions.yaml + target-version semantics"; "subsumed by discovery-document check" applies to removal only); design §2.4 severity mapping.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a small built-in deprecation table (pluto semantics, refreshed per k8s minor) for served-but-deprecated versions; derive removal from discovery.

findings.section: §3.5 snapshot format wording ("1.37 static-manifest form for VAP/MAP") and export adapters
findings.claim_or_choice: Store VAP/MAP in the 1.37 static-manifest form; export to KWOK/envtest/static admission layouts.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Static manifests forbid `paramKind`/`paramRef`, while the imported cluster policies commonly use params; the stored form is just v1 YAML, and an export to a static-admission directory must strip or rewrite param bindings (and inject the param objects into the target cluster) or the apiserver rejects the bundle.
findings.evidence: fidelity brief §2 (static policies: "spec.paramKind/paramRef not allowed", `.static.k8s.io` naming); design §3.5 layer text.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 YAML (v1beta1 on 1.34/1.35)"; make the static-manifest export a lossy adapter that documents dropped param bindings.

findings.section: §3.5 slices ("developer-safe" includes `admission/policies/ + params` and `engines/`)
findings.claim_or_choice: VAP/MAP params and engine policies are developer-safe.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Param ConfigMaps/CRs and Kyverno/Gatekeeper policies routinely embed customer-specific allow-lists (registries, hostnames, CIDRs, tenant names) — the kind of data the confidential `full` slice is meant to withhold from developers.
findings.evidence: design §3.5 layer table; Kyverno external-data-sources pattern (allow-lists in ConfigMaps consumed by policies).
findings.suggested_fix: Route param objects and policy CRs through the same tested redaction layer with an operator allow/deny list before they enter the developer-safe slice; default params to `full`.

what_is_right: No `k8s.io/kubernetes` module and no `replace` directives: `k8s.io/apiserver`, `apiextensions-apiserver`, `pod-security-admission`, Helm v4.3.0, kustomize/api, jsonschema/v6, compose-go, oras-go all co-resolve at v0.37.0 without replaces (embed brief §0.1, §2, §5) — keep this constraint, and keep OPA/gatekeeper out of go.mod until Rego is actually evaluated.

Kyverno by subprocess, digest-pinned per snapshot engine version, with zhi-owned exit codes: the PSA fork replace, ~416 requires and 2026 CVE cadence (embed brief §0.4, §1) make in-process embedding the wrong call; the CLI flags the design relies on (`--context-file`, `--parameter-resource`, `--userinfo`, `--policy-report`) are confirmed from source (embed brief §4.2).

CRD validation through kubectl-validate's `customresource.NewStrategy` path is exactly the server's: strategy.go at release-1.37 builds `cel.NewValidator(structuralSchema, true, celconfig.PerCallLimit)` and validates with `celconfig.RuntimeCELCostBudget`; the `NewStrategy` signature is unchanged 1.35→1.37, so the pseudo-version pin is workable.

Native types labelled `approximate`, CRDs `exact`: KEP-5073 explicitly does not publish validation rules to OpenAPI (fidelity brief §1), so the design's refusal to claim apiserver-exact native validation is correct and must survive revision.

`MustBaseEnvSet(ver *version.Version)` with one pinned minor and a skew Warning for newer clusters is the right version strategy (signature confirmed at v0.37.0; downward emulation via IntroducedVersion/RemovedVersion per embed brief §2).

Helm v4 SDK feeds: `RenderWithClientProvider(chrt, values, ClientProvider)` exists for snapshot-backed `lookup`, and `Engine.CustomTemplateFuncs` exists — the determinism fix is available inside the chosen SDK, so the Helm-as-real-engine decision stands.

PSA cluster defaults/exemptions as `declared, not observed` with vendor presets (no `/configz`; EKS/GKE privileged-no-exemptions; OpenShift bindata) and namespace-label evaluation via `k8s.io/pod-security-admission/policy` — matches fidelity brief §8.
MAP `v1` on ≥1.36 with `v1beta1` fallback on 1.34/1.35 and `featureState` recorded in manifest.json — matches fidelity brief §3.

Own snapshot format rather than `kwokctl snapshot export`: the kwok default filter excludes CRDs, VAP/MAP, webhooks, ResourceQuota and classes (fidelity brief §7); kubectl-validate layout for OpenAPI with `?hash=` keying and export adapters is the right interop shape.

Consuming Gatekeeper's generated VAP/VAPB (beta, default-on since v3.20, k8s ≥1.30) instead of re-implementing the engine, and reporting Rego templates as "not evaluated" until OPA is embedded — honest and consistent with fidelity brief §6.

Argo CD's pre-sync feedback really is weaker than people assume (SSD opt-in, skips new resources, excludes mutation webhooks; 120 s + 60 s jitter), so the pre-push wedge is additive, not redundant (fidelity brief §5).

Severity mapping (Deny/Enforce/schema/CEL → Blocking; Warn/Audit/dryrun/PSA warn-audit/webhook match/stale quota → Warning; deprecation/annotations → Info) and honouring PolicyExceptions/enforcementAction matches every brief's recommendation.
Unknowns are never Blocking; `--strict` promotes them to Warnings in CI; `declared.yaml` for unobservable inputs; `unobserved[]` in the Finding type — right shape for offline ≠ online.

Zero loadable plugins in v1, `check/v1` as a digest-pinned exec contract, no proto/go-plugin/marketplace until a second implementor exists — consistent with the audit's measured plugin cost and with how Argo/Flux/Kyverno/Kubewarden actually extend.
Webhook match prediction as a first-class unknown with vendor-webhook claiming (cert-manager, kyverno-svc, gatekeeper) to avoid double counting — matches cluster-state-import brief implication 6.
Snapshots in OCI with slices and tested redaction, committed directory only for air-gap; reports never committed; kubeconfigs and tokens never persisted.

JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) addressing, yaml.v3 positions, comment-preserving write-back of touched leaves only, machine-owned pointers read-only — the right domain-model choices given the audit's findings on the flat path model.
Immutable-field checks labelled `approximate` for native types and `exact` only for CRD `oldSelf` rules — correctly walks back pr-native's over-claim.
Cutting order that keeps the form last and shipping CLI → bot → form: consistent with the persona split and with the evidence that validators outside the push path (Monokle, Datree) died.

lens: Consultant deploying vendor software into customer clusters (day-1 realities: read-only RBAC, air gap, GitLab, no schema, Compose-only, no PR review) alternating with a Helm-chart-authoring developer (will I author schemas/CEL, what does the transition cost me) — refuting the UX and workflow, not the engine.
verdict: Nothing here is fatal: the skeleton — Git-only writes, CLI+bot before form, contract in standard shapes plus a deployer-owned overlay, signed snapshot with fidelity in the finding record, shallow plugins — is the right shape and is well evidenced. What is under-specified is the layer between the pure pipeline and the two humans. The flagship consultant example in §1.3 ("restricted-v2 will reject runAsUser: 1000" phrased against the field they touched) is exactly the finding §3.7 admits cannot be back-mapped, and v1 ships neither suppressions nor a workaround path, so the consultant's first Blocking on a vendor chart is a dead end and the check gets disabled. The form has no notion of which values layer a change should land in. The "editor for free" modeline will produce false `required` errors on every layered file, while the emitted schema could absorb most of the form's unique value (cluster pickers as resolved enums) — S9 measures renderability, not the residual. Day 1 at a real customer: the `full` slice needs `list secrets` (which is full secret read), the default OCI+cosign distribution needs a registry, a signing identity and an approved ClusterRole that do not exist in week one, `.zhi/snapshots` is labelled an "exception" when it is the only feasible first path, plain-Helm/helmfile layouts (the most common vendor-install shape) are absent from §5.1, and `ref://`→ExternalSecret write-back cannot work on a single-Helm-source Argo Application. The transition story contradicts itself: bot-mode safety (`allowExec`, `maxAge`) lives in a file whose ownership the transition explicitly moves to the PR author. Compose — named by the owner as a peer target — gets zero spikes and lands around month 13 when a schema+strict-interpolation T0-a is a two-week add. Fix these and the design is buildable and adoptable; ship it as written and the consultant's first month is worse than the CLI stack they already have.

findings.section: §1.3 Consultants and supporters / §3.7 Lineage / §10.3 Phase 2 (suppressions)
findings.claim_or_choice: §1.3 promises findings "phrased against the field they touched with the policy cited: 'restricted-v2 SCC will reject runAsUser: 1000'"; §3.7 concedes Helm emits no source map and that findings without a values pointer are tagged developer-side; §10.3 puts baselines/suppressions in phase 2.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: `runAsUser` on vendor charts is almost always hard-coded in the template (or a nested `podSecurityContext` object with no `x-zhi-targets`), so the design's own headline example arrives as a developer-side finding anchored on a rendered Pod, not on a field. The consultant then has a Blocking finding on a chart they cannot change, no suppression/baseline mechanism until phase 2, no patch layer (Kustomize patch write-back is phase 2), and `zhi propose`/`zhi check` semantics for a known-accepted Blocking are unspecified. Native-type validation is also labelled `approximate` (§3.4), so false-positive Blockings will occur. A validator with false positives and no override is the one that gets disabled — the fate of every stalled tool in the post-mortems.
findings.evidence: Design §1.3, §3.7 (feasibility lens fatal flaw 2), §3.4 T0-a `approximate` for native types, §10.3 "baselines/suppressions" in phase 2; report §3.1 class 3 (native types approximate) and §3.3 (Kyverno #5476 offline≠online); competitors brief Task C (Datree/Monokle: validation outside the push path or with no deploy story dies); devops-pain-points brief pain evidence on Kyverno v1.12 CI green on violations (the opposite failure — teams route around checks).
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Move `.zhi/suppressions.yaml` (finding-id hash from §2.4, reason, owner, expiry, `side`) into M1; `zhi check` treats a suppressed Blocking as Warning and prints it in the PR table. (2) Rewrite §1.3's example to one that back-maps today (`persistence.storageClass` RWX, `ingress.className`) and state plainly that pod-security findings on vendor charts land developer-side. (3) Give the consultant a v1 workaround path for developer-side findings: the overlay may add `x-zhi-targets` and a `proposedValue`, and `zhi explain` prints the chart values key(s) that influence the flagged rendered pointer via fingerprint match. (4) Specify `zhi propose --allow-blocking` (default refuse) so the CLI matches the UI's refuse-on-Blocking contract.

findings.section: §3.2 Edit → PR data flow step (4) / §5.2 PR production / §3.6 UI stack
findings.claim_or_choice: "Propose writes only touched leaves through the yaml.v3 tree" and "one commit per proposal touching only human-owned layers"; the form edits effective values and shows the source layer per leaf.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The design discovers a layer stack (`chart defaults < common < variant < env < cluster < runtime < machine-managed`, §2.2) but never says which file a form edit is written to. A consultant changing `replicaCount` for eu-prod must choose between `common/values.yaml` (all envs) and `envs/eu-prod/values.yaml` (this env); writing to the leaf's current source layer is wrong half the time (a value currently coming from `common` that should now be env-specific). The form↔YAML toggle (Devtron's idea) is equally undefined: which file does the YAML pane show? This is the Rancher "Edit as YAML is NOT the values.yaml" two-sources-of-truth trap the persona brief warns about, reintroduced through layering.
findings.evidence: Design §2.2 Values layer entity, §3.2 step 4, §5.2, §3.6 "form ↔ YAML toggle"; report §3.1 class 16 (wrong effective value across merge layers: "you need to manually run Helm in your head"); environments-secrets-drift brief implication 4 (layering model with source layer) and pain evidence "Rancher: yaml shown upon Edit as YAML ... is NOT the Values.yaml" (platform-engineering brief).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a target-layer concept to the session API and CLI: each edit carries `writeTo: <layer>` defaulting to the environment layer for `zhi ui --env X` and to the leaf's current human-owned source layer when that is more specific; show a per-field "currently from: common/values.yaml → will write to: envs/eu-prod/values.yaml" affordance; refuse writes to machine-owned layers (already read-only). The YAML pane shows the selected target layer file, not the effective tree. Add this to S6 (round-trip) so it is tested on the company's real layered files.

findings.section: §3.8 CLI, CI, LSP, MCP ("Editor for free in v1") / §3.6 Form generation (S9)
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi contract emit` writes `.zhi/schema.json` and injects the `# yaml-language-server: $schema=` modeline into managed values files; the form is justified by typed widgets and cluster-aware pickers; S9 passes at ≥95 % leaves typed.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Two problems. (a) Helm validates the schema against the FINAL merged `.Values`, so the contract legitimately carries `required`; attaching that same schema via modeline to a partial overlay file (`common/values.yaml`, `envs/prod/values.yaml`) makes yaml-language-server flag every missing required key in every layer file — the "free" editor integration ships as noise on exactly the layered layout §5.1 discovers. (b) The question "is the form better than YAML+LSP" is never tested. Once the schema is emitted, VS Code already gives enums, types, descriptions and completion; the form's unique value reduces to snapshot pickers, persona grouping/hiding, and inline rendered-stage findings (which §3.7 says are weak). Pickers can be delivered into the editor for free by resolving `x-zhi-cluster-ref` into an `enum` per environment at emit time. S9's 95 %-typed criterion measures renderability of Bitnami shapes, not whether a consultant completes a change faster or with fewer errors than with editor+modeline+`zhi validate`.
findings.evidence: Design §3.8, §3.6 S9 criterion, §4 `x-zhi-cluster-ref`; environments-secrets-drift brief ("values.schema.json ... validated against the FINAL merged .Values"); schema-validation-tech brief (yaml-language-server modeline behaviour, RJSF live validation cost); persona brief pain evidence (KubeForge "no guidance whatsoever" is about a GUI YAML editor, not a form) and implication 5 (pickers from the snapshot); owner ask explicitly requires a UI, so the question is investment/ordering, not existence.
findings.suggested_fix: (a) `zhi contract emit` must write two schemas: the merged contract for `.zhi/schema.json` and a `partial` variant (strip `required`, keep `additionalProperties`/types/enums) whose modeline goes into layer files; per-environment variants resolve `x-zhi-cluster-ref` to `enum` from the snapshot so pickers exist in any editor in M1. (b) Add a task-based arm to S14: three consultants perform the same two changes (RWX storage class; enable ingress with class) via editor+modeline+`zhi validate` and via the S9 prototype form; record time, errors, and which surface they would keep. (c) Re-state the form's justification as the residual over the editor path (visibility map, persona grouping, inline rendered findings) and make that residual the S9 go/no-go alongside the 95 % criterion.

findings.section: §1.3 first-hour path / §4 Deployer overlay (`zhi contract init` synthesis)
findings.claim_or_choice: When the chart ships no schema, one is "synthesised from `values.yaml` defaults and `# @schema` comments" into the overlay, and the form then opens with cluster-aware pickers.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Synthesis from defaults cannot produce the two things that make day 1 worthwhile on a schema-less chart. (1) Unknown-key detection: the most common values error is a typo'd or renamed key (`replicacount`, `ingress.class` vs `ingress.className`) that Helm silently ignores; a synthesised schema with default `additionalProperties` (true) catches none of it, and `additionalProperties:false` everywhere breaks free-form maps (`extraEnv`, `podAnnotations`). Distinguishing the two requires extracting `.Values.*` references from the templates — a known technique the devops brief names and the design omits. (2) Pickers: `x-zhi-cluster-ref` is an annotation only a human adds; `storageClass: ""` infers to `string`. So the promised pickers on Bitnami-class charts appear only after the consultant hand-annotates the overlay, which contradicts "zero developer cooperation, first hour".
findings.evidence: Design §1.3 and §4 synthesis description; devops-pain-points brief implication 4 ("infer from template usage + rendered-output schema"); platform-engineering brief pain evidence (Bitnami redis schema has descriptions/defaults only, no enum/x-* hints); k8s-config-languages brief (losisin/dadav synthesize from `# @schema` comments only); persona brief implication 5 (Rancher `storageclass`/`secret` pickers are the copy-worthy feature).
findings.suggested_fix: Specify synthesis as three passes: (1) defaults + `# @schema`/`## @param`/helm-docs comments; (2) template reference extraction (`.Values.a.b.c`, `index .Values`, `with/range` scopes, subchart `global`) to mark objects `additionalProperties:false` where every child is referenced and leave maps used via `range`/`toYaml` open — unknown keys surface as Warning with `keywordLocation` pointing at the nearest known sibling; (3) naming heuristics for cluster refs (`storageClass(Name)?` → storageclass, `ingressClassName|ingress.className` → ingressclass, `existingSecret|secretName|*.secretKeyRef` → secret-key, `serviceAccount.name`, `priorityClassName`, `runtimeClassName`, `image.registry|repository` → image). Add a spike line to S9: on Bitnami redis and two internal charts, report the share of deployer-touched leaves that get a picker from heuristics alone.

findings.section: §3.5 Snapshot format (`inventory/`, `full` slice, `zhi snapshot rbac`) / §1.3 first-hour path
findings.claim_or_choice: `inventory/` holds "names+keys only" of Secrets; `zhi snapshot rbac --slice full` emits a minimal ClusterRole a bank's security team can review; the first-hour path runs with that read-only identity.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: There is no Kubernetes RBAC grant for Secret names or keys without values: `get`, `list` and `watch` on `secrets` all return full contents, and the keys live in `data`. The generated ClusterRole therefore asks a bank for cluster-wide secret read — the rule the reviewer strikes first — so the `full` slice's secret inventory, the `x-zhi-cluster-ref: secret-key` picker, class 10 (missing Secret key) and the `ref://` store-presence Blocking will be absent at most regulated customers. The design describes per-layer degradation in `manifest.json` but not the resulting UX (what the picker shows, what severity the reference check gets). Separately, even the `developer-safe` slice needs cluster-scoped list rights on CRDs, VAP/MAP, Kyverno policies and StorageClasses; a consultant's usual namespace-scoped `view`/`edit` binding yields discovery + OpenAPI v3 only, and getting a ClusterRole approved takes weeks. The design has no named mode for that interval.
findings.evidence: Kubernetes RBAC good practices, "Listing secrets": "`list` and `watch` access also effectively allow for users to reveal the Secret contents" (https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/, checked 2026-09-13); design §3.5 layer table and `zhi snapshot rbac`; cluster-state-import brief implication 2 ("degrades gracefully recording forbidden layers") and its RBAC note that OpenAPI v3 for CRDs is served without listing CRDs; deployer brief Part 2 (security-review expectations).
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Be explicit in §3.5 that `inventory/secrets` requires full secret read and is expected to be refused; make the importer's Secret pass optional and namespace-scoped (`--namespaces`), and define the degraded UX: `secret-key` picker becomes free text with an `unobserved: ["inventory:secrets"]` badge, class 10 and `ref://` store checks report `unobserved` (Warning under `--strict`), never Blocking.
