(2) Define a supported "discovery-only" import tier (discovery + `/openapi/v3` + version) that yields T0-a (schema, removed APIs, CRD CEL from the OpenAPI document) with any authenticated identity, so the consultant gets value before the ClusterRole lands; record it as `slice: discovery`. (3) Have `zhi snapshot rbac` emit two ClusterRoles (cluster-scoped read; namespaced read incl. secrets) so the security reviewer can approve the first and scope the second.

findings.section: §0 item 7 / §3.5 Snapshot format (OCI default, cosign v3 signing "never cut", committed directory as "the air-gap exception") / §5.6 bot-mode security
findings.claim_or_choice: Snapshots default to an OCI registry with cosign v3 signing verified by an exec'd digest-pinned cosign; `.zhi/snapshots/<env>/` is an exception for air gap; every exec binary is pulled by digest from OCI.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: On day 1 at a customer the consultant has none of: a registry the confidential `full` slice may be pushed to (the consultancy's registry means customer data leaves the customer, which §3.5 itself forbids; the customer's registry needs a push grant), a signing identity (keyless signing needs Fulcio + OIDC + Rekor/TSA online; key-based needs a managed key), or a way for the customer's CI runner to pull the Kyverno CLI/cosign binaries from OCI in an air-gapped or egress-restricted environment. The design's default path is therefore the *last* one a consultant can use, and the path they can use is labelled an exception, with air-gap export/import deferred to phase 3 "until a regulated buyer exists" — but the consultancy's customers are that buyer. GitLab (the self-hosted SCM those customers overwhelmingly run) is phase 2 and in the cut list, so `zhi check` with trailer/digest matching is GitHub-only for a year.
findings.evidence: Design §0.7, §3.5, §5.6, §7 (air-gap phase 3), §10.3 (GitLab phase 2), §0.3 cut order; deployer brief Part 2 item 7 ("Keyless signing needs Fulcio + an OIDC issuer + (Rekor or TSA) — impossible fully offline") and item 8 (mirrors for snapshots/plugins); persona brief (Replicated air-gap bundles; consultants install into customer-owned clusters); §3.5 says the full slice is customer-confidential.
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Make the local/committed snapshot directory a first-class, non-exceptional path in M1: `zhi snapshot import` writes to `.zhi/cache/`, `zhi snapshot commit --env X` writes the directory (or a Git-LFS blob) into the customer's GitOps repo, `zhi.lock` pins its digest; signing is `optional` with a `signed: false` Warning in the PR header until a registry/key exists. (2) Support a `bin/` directory alongside `zhi.lock` where adapter binaries are matched by digest without OCI access; ship `zhi bundle export/import` (tarball of snapshot + adapters + profiles) in M1 as the minimal air-gap story — it is the carried `zhi-mirror` bundle format, not new code. (3) State explicitly that `zhi validate --exit-code --format md` is the SCM-agnostic CI path (works in GitLab CI/Jenkins today) and that Check Run + SARIF + trailer digest are the GitHub bot's extras; move a minimal GitLab commit-status + MR-note adapter (small API) into months 5–6 or document the workaround.

findings.section: §5.1 Discovery (`internal/layout`)
findings.claim_or_choice: `internal/layout` reads only what Argo CD, Flux and Kargo read; layouts are folder-per-env, app-of-apps/ApplicationSet, rendered-manifest branches; branch-per-env is read-only legacy.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: A large share of vendor-into-customer deployments have no GitOps controller at all: values in Git, `helm upgrade -f` (or helmfile) run from CI or by hand — Replicated, the reference implementation for this persona, recommends plain Helm for customer-managed clusters and 67 % of vendors use Helm as the primary install. With no controller CRs the layer stack cannot be discovered, so the consultant must hand-write every binding in `.zhi/workspace.yaml` ("overridden here") with no documented shape, and `zhi check`'s "every environment whose files changed" has no file→environment map. The same gap hits Compose in phase 2, where the "controller" is a CI job over SSH.
findings.evidence: Design §5.1 and §2.2 Workspace ("most fields discovered from Argo/Flux CRs, overridden here"); persona brief summary and tools table (Replicated "recommends plain Helm for customer-managed clusters"; State of Self-Hosted 2025: 67 % Helm primary); environments-secrets-drift brief (Helmfile 1.7.4 "remains the pragmatic environments + values + SOPS secrets tool" with a stated precedence list); docker-compose brief (CI is `config -q` then `up` over SSH, not controllers).
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `plain` layout to §5.1 for M1: explicit `packages[].environments[].valueFiles` (ordered, last wins) in `.zhi/workspace.yaml`, plus a `helmfile` reader (environments, values, precedence per the brief). `zhi env import` should propose the binding from the CI file it finds (`helm upgrade ... -f a.yaml -f b.yaml` in `.gitlab-ci.yml`/workflows) with a confirmation step, the same UX as controller discovery.

findings.section: §2.2 Secret reference entity / §10.2 M1 ("ESO `ref://` rendering with store-presence check")
findings.claim_or_choice: `ref://<store>/<path>#<key>` is never a value and is "rendered to ESO `ExternalSecret` v1" in M1.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Rendering an `ExternalSecret` means writing a new manifest into the GitOps repo, not a values leaf. On the most common layout the design targets — an Argo Application with a single Helm source — Argo "only uses Helm to inflate charts with `helm template`", so a sibling `ExternalSecret` file next to the values files is never applied; it needs a multi-source Application, a Kustomize wrapper, or a Flux Kustomization beside the HelmRelease. Vendor charts consume `existingSecret: <name>` (Bitnami convention), so the deployer's real workflow is: ensure an `ExternalSecret` exists (via the platform team or a separate app) and point the chart at its name. The design's write-back therefore either silently produces an unapplied file or requires a layout change the consultant cannot make.
findings.evidence: Argo CD Helm user guide: "Helm is only used to inflate charts with helm template" (https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/helm/, checked 2026-09-13); Argo multiple-sources page frames combining a chart with other sources as the multi-source use case; design §2.2, §10.2; environments-secrets-drift brief implication 5 (ESO reference model; Blocking if store missing; Warning if key missing); persona brief tools table (Bitnami `existingSecret` pattern in troubleshooting docs).
findings.suggested_fix: In M1, `ref://` is a validation-time type only: the form's `x-zhi-secret` input resolves to the chart's existing-secret convention (`existingSecret`/`secretName` + key) and the pipeline checks store presence, secret name and key against the snapshot inventory (degrading to `unobserved` per the RBAC finding). Emitting `ExternalSecret` manifests becomes a layout-aware capability: only when `internal/layout` can prove a manifests path is applied for that environment (multi-source Application, Kustomize dir, Flux Kustomization); otherwise the PR body carries the `ExternalSecret` as a snippet for the platform team. Move that emission to months 5–6 alongside the overlay.

findings.section: §3.2 step (5) / §5.4 The bot is the product
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi check` re-validates the PR head and "its report digest must equal the trailer's or the check fails with 'report mismatch'".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The trailer is written at `zhi propose` time. Any later commit on the same PR — the reviewer's suggestion, the author fixing a comment in their editor, a Renovate rebase — changes the report digest, so the check fails on every hand-edited zhi PR until the author re-runs `zhi propose`. That penalises exactly the editor/LSP path the design also promotes, and it turns a provenance feature into a workflow tax. Renovate/Kargo PRs carry no trailers at all, so "validated uniformly" already implies the check must run without a trailer; the mismatch rule as written is therefore neither necessary for those nor tolerable for humans.
findings.evidence: Design §3.2 step 5, §5.2 trailers, §5.4; engine-first §6 as cited in the design (byte-identical digests across surfaces is a *pipeline* property, not a PR-immutability property); environments-secrets-drift brief pain evidence (machine edits and rebases on values files are routine: Image Updater, Renovate).
findings.suggested_fix: Redefine the rule: the check always recomputes on the PR head and posts the fresh report; if a `Zhi-Report` trailer exists on the head commit and matches, mark "reproduced"; if it differs, mark "trailer stale (report recomputed)" as Info. Fail only on integrity mismatches — `Zhi-Snapshot`/`Zhi-Contract`/`Zhi-Profile` digests that differ from `zhi.lock` on the head (tampering or an un-locked bump), or a snapshot older than `maxAge`. Keep byte-identical digests as the test-suite invariant across surfaces.

findings.section: §3.5 Snapshot freshness ("refuse at load time ... refuse to clear Blocking on a snapshot older than the environment's maxAge") / §1.5 third role
findings.claim_or_choice: Freshness is a lockfile property: `zhi open` refuses to load, and `zhi check` refuses to clear Blocking, when the snapshot exceeds `maxAge`; refresh is a platform team's scheduled job.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: At a customer there is no cooperating platform team on day 1 and often no standing identity for a scheduled job; the consultant imports from a laptop when on site (weekly at best, often monthly). With a single `maxAge`, a visiting consultant's check is permanently red and `zhi open` refuses to even show the form — so the consultant lowers `maxAge` to a year or turns the check off. The staleness that matters differs by layer: `ResourceQuota.status.used` is stale in hours (already Warning-graded in §3.3 step 9), CRDs/policies change in weeks, discovery in months. The research recommended warning on age, not refusing.
findings.evidence: Design §3.5 (refuse), §1.5, §3.3 step 9; cluster-state-import brief implication 10 ("warn on age > N days or stale quota; hash-addressed OpenAPI keeps refresh cheap"); environments-secrets-drift brief implication 10 ("refuse Blocking-clear on stale snapshots" — the design took this and dropped the per-layer nuance); persona brief §4 (consultant/supporter cadence; instances at customers, not a fleet the vendor operates).
findings.suggested_fix: Per-layer `maxAge` with sane defaults (quota status: 24 h → Warning; namespaces/inventory: 7 d → Warning; policies/CRDs/discovery: 90 d → Warning; anything beyond a hard `maxAge` → the check posts Warning "snapshot N days old" and clears Blocking only with `--allow-stale` in the environment file). `zhi open` never refuses; it badges. Add `zhi snapshot refresh --layers quota,namespaces` as a cheap partial re-import (hash-addressed OpenAPI already makes this cheap) so a consultant with a namespace-scoped identity can refresh the layers that go stale fastest.

findings.section: §1.5 The third role and the transition / §5.6 Bot-mode security
findings.claim_or_choice: "The transition changes no artifact ... What changes is a CODEOWNERS line"; and "exec renderers and external checks are denied in `zhi check` unless listed in the environment's `allowExec` allowlist, which lives in `.zhi/environments/<env>.yaml` owned by the deployer side per CODEOWNERS, not by the PR author."
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: These two sentences contradict each other. The moment developers own their environment (the transition's goal), they own `.zhi/environments/<env>.yaml` and therefore `allowExec`, `maxAge`, `allowDirectPush`, the snapshot registry and the profile — i.e. the PR author now controls the bot's arbitrary-code allowlist and the staleness gate. The security argument of §5.6 (ecosystem lens fatal flaw 2) rests on a CODEOWNERS split that the transition erases. The same file mixes platform policy with environment binding, so there is no way to hand over one without the other.
findings.evidence: Design §1.5, §5.6, §2.2 Environment entity (fields: `allowDirectPush`, `allowExec`, snapshot ref + `maxAge`, profile id); contract-first §2 as cited (platform team as third role); report §7.3 (bot evaluates PR-controlled inputs).
findings.suggested_fix: Split the environment into two files with different owners: `.zhi/environments/<env>.yaml` (binding: targets, namespaces, GitOps CR refs, values paths, matrix dimensions — owned by whoever deploys) and `.zhi/policy/<env>.yaml` or a workspace-level `policy:` block (allowExec, allowDirectPush, maxAge, profile pin, snapshot registry, strict default — owned by the platform/security side, never by the PR author). `zhi check` reads policy only from the base branch, not the PR head, so a PR cannot loosen its own gate. This preserves "only a CODEOWNERS line moves" for the binding while keeping the safety envelope fixed.

findings.section: §1.2 Developers / §3.5 developer-safe slice / §10.2 M1
findings.claim_or_choice: Developers "run `zhi validate --env dev` against the dev cluster snapshot in their own PRs" and "never need cluster access"; the `developer-safe` slice (discovery, OpenAPI, CRDs, VAP/MAP, engines/, webhooks metadata, catalogs) "lets developers validate against a customer's dev cluster" and "crosses the invisible border".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Three gaps. (1) In the chart/app repo there is no `.zhi/workspace.yaml` and no environment (those live in the GitOps repo), so `zhi validate --env dev` as described has nothing to bind to until `zhi contract test` with fixture snapshots arrives in months 5–6; M1 delivers nothing developers can run. (2) The developer-safe slice includes `engines/` (every Kyverno/Gatekeeper policy), `admission/policies/` and the CRD list — a customer's complete security posture and installed-operator inventory. A bank will not approve that leaving for a vendor's GitHub CI; "developer-safe" is not "customer-safe". (3) For the transition, a developer deploying to their own namespace needs the `full` slice for that namespace (quota, PSA labels, existing secrets) but nothing else; the slices are binary {developer-safe, full} with no namespace-scoped cut, so the transition either over-shares or under-validates.
findings.evidence: Design §1.2, §1.5, §3.5 layer table (`engines/` and `admission/policies/` marked developer-safe), §10.2 (contract tooling months 5–6); deployer brief Part 2 (regulated review expectations; "no telemetry, offline"); cluster-state-import brief implication 2 (`--filter` by workspace namespaces exists as an importer concept); persona brief implication 9 (same artifact, two surfaces).
findings.suggested_fix: (1) Define the chart-repo workspace shape in §2.2: a minimal `zhi.yaml` in the chart repo binding `package: .` to `fixtures: [profile://openshift-4.20, profile://vanilla-1.37, snapshot://...]`, so M1's `zhi validate --fixture profile://openshift-4.20` works for developers without any customer data — profiles double as synthetic snapshots (default SCCs, `restricted` PSA, common quotas). (2) Re-tier the slices: `schema` (discovery, OpenAPI, CRDs, catalogs' class names) is the border-crossing default; `policy` (engines/, admission/) requires explicit customer approval recorded in `manifest.json`; `full` stays confidential. (3) Add a `namespaces: [..]` filter producing a namespace-scoped `full` slice for the transition case. Ship (1) in M1 — it is the only developer-facing deliverable before month 5.

findings.section: §6 Docker Compose path (phase 2) / §10.1 Spike sprint / §0 item 3 cut order
findings.claim_or_choice: Compose lands in phase 2 (+4–5 months after month 8), "the domain model is target-agnostic from day one so Compose lands without a migration"; Compose is in the schedule-pressure cut list; S1–S15 contain no Compose spike.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The owner named Compose as a peer target and the company's developers author Compose deployments; a Compose-only customer gets nothing from zhi for roughly a year, and "target-agnostic" is asserted without a single spike touching compose-go, the `{file, service}` resource identity, or a host snapshot layer. Meanwhile the cheap half of Compose value needs no host snapshot at all: the 2020-12 Compose schema plus ~28 consistency checks plus strict interpolation (unset variable → Blocking) plus a form over `ExtractVariables` — the research says "the schema is already good enough to drive a generated form; what is missing is everything that depends on the target host".
findings.evidence: Owner ask ("especially in Kubernetes and in Docker Compose"); design §6, §10.1, §0.3; docker-compose brief state-of-slice and implications 1–2 (compose-go `ExtractVariables`, strict interpolation, `config -q` blind spots) and pain evidence (unset variables silently become ""); report §3.1 class 17; §8 "what nobody does" item 5 (Compose first-class).
findings.suggested_fix: Add S16 (two days): load a real company Compose project with compose-go, run `ExtractVariables`, emit a `values.schema.json` over the variables, produce three findings (`${VAR:?}` unset, unknown `x-` key, `deploy.*` with swarm=false) in the `pkg/report` shape with `{file, service}` identity — pass criterion is that no domain-model field has to change. Then schedule a "Compose T0-a" slice (schema + consistency + strict interpolation + variables form + `.env`/`compose.<env>.yaml` write-back, no host snapshot) in months 5–6 (~1.5k LOC on compose-go) and keep the host snapshot and policy pack in phase 2. Remove Compose from the cut list or state that Compose-only customers are out of scope for year one.

findings.section: §1.2 Developers / §4 contract / §10.2 roadmap
findings.claim_or_choice: Developers own the contract (`values.schema.json` + `x-zhi-*`, `values.cel.yaml`, `zhi/requirements.yaml`) and run `zhi contract lint|test` in chart CI.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Evidence says developers rarely author even `values.schema.json` ("just vibes"; Bitnami ships descriptions only). The developer's zhi-independent payoff is limited to the schema (Helm 4 enforces it) and the emitted Preflight Secret; `values.cel.yaml` and `x-zhi-*` only pay off through zhi or the tiny helm-cel plugin. The design's honest answer is the overlay (deployers author what developers did not), which is right, but §1.4's "developers stop shipping charts that assume privileged dev clusters" is a deployer benefit — the developer's own incentive is never stated, and the contract tooling arrives at months 5–6, after the bot has been nagging developer-side findings for two months with no tool to fix them.
findings.evidence: devops-pain-points brief ("values.yaml has no type schema, just vibes"; schema "optional and rare"); platform-engineering brief pain evidence (Bitnami redis schema without hints); k8s-config-languages brief ("many popular charts don't ship" a schema); design §1.2, §1.4, §10.2.
findings.suggested_fix: Give developers one thing in M1 that is useful without zhi: `zhi contract emit` producing a Helm-4-valid `values.schema.json` from the synthesis passes (typed, `additionalProperties` decisions, descriptions) and a helm-cel-runnable `values.cel.yaml` skeleton — so the first developer-side finding from the bot arrives with a one-command fix. State the developer incentive in §1.4 as "fewer support tickets across the border" and let the `side: developer` count per chart in the PR table make it visible.

findings.section: §5.2 PR production / §5.4 ("posts a GitHub Check Run + SARIF")
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi check` posts a Check Run and SARIF; branch protection can require it.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: SARIF upload to code scanning is only available on private/internal repositories when GitHub Code Security is enabled (a paid add-on on Enterprise); most customer GitOps repos are private. Check Run annotations work with a GitHub App or Actions token alone.
findings.evidence: GitHub docs, "Uploading a SARIF file to GitHub": "For private and internal repositories, code scanning is available when GitHub Code Security features are enabled for the repository" (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/integrating-with-code-scanning/uploading-a-sarif-file-to-github, checked 2026-09-13).
findings.suggested_fix: Make Check Run annotations (file:line from yaml.v3 positions, ≤50 per run — batch) the primary surface and SARIF an optional `--sarif` output; mention the licensing gate in the docs so a consultant does not spend a day on a 403.

findings.section: §4 (a) `values.schema.json` — `x-zhi-targets` example / §3.7 lineage (b)
findings.claim_or_choice: `"x-zhi-targets": ["/spec/volumeClaimTemplates/0/spec/storageClassName"]` — a bare JSON Pointer into "the rendered document".
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: A chart renders many documents; the same value may land at different pointers in a Deployment vs a StatefulSet, and a pointer without a resource selector is ambiguous the moment a chart has two workloads. Glasskube's `targets` (the cited inspiration) carried a target identifier plus a patch path. As a chart author I cannot write this correctly as specified, and S10 cannot measure coverage of an underspecified field.
findings.evidence: Design §4 example and vocabulary list; persona brief contract pattern 1 (Glasskube `targets: [{chartName, patch: {op, path}}]`).
findings.suggested_fix: Define `x-zhi-targets` entries as `{kind, name?: glob, pointer}` (name defaulting to any), allow `apiVersion` optionally, and let `zhi contract lint` verify each target resolves in a rendered fixture. Document that pointers use RFC 6901 with `~1` escaping (already stated in §2.1).

findings.section: §4 (b) `values.cel.yaml` (`env.storageClasses`, `snapshot` at stage 17)
findings.claim_or_choice: Rules reference `env.storageClasses.exists(sc, sc.name == ... && sc.rwxCapable == true)` and, at stage 17, `rendered` and `snapshot`.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: CEL is statically typed; authors need the declared types of `env`, `snapshot`, `rendered`, `values`, `oldValues` (fields, list element types, the `unknown` tri-state for `rwxCapable`) or every rule is trial-and-error. The design never lists them, and "the contract documents which variables are available in which stage" is not the same as a published type schema.
findings.evidence: Design §3.3 stage 1 and 17, §4 (b); schema-validation-tech brief (cel-go static type-check, `k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/environment`); report §9 #12 (CEL as the single rule language with the VAP variable set).
findings.suggested_fix: Publish `pkg/report`-style versioned CEL type declarations (`zhi.dev/cel/v1`: `Env{name, storageClasses[]{name, provisioner, rwxCapable: 'true'|'false'|'unknown', isDefault}, ingressClasses[], namespaces[], profile}`, `Snapshot{...}`, `Rendered{objects[]}`) and have `zhi contract lint` type-check every rule against them; ship a `zhi contract cel-doc` that prints the declarations.

findings.section: §2.2 Component entity ("mapped to Helm `condition`, Kustomize `Component`, Compose `profiles`")
findings.claim_or_choice: `x-zhi-component` toggles map to Helm `condition`.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Helm `condition`/`tags` apply only to subchart dependencies declared in `Chart.yaml`; an in-chart feature toggle (`ingress.enabled`, `metrics.enabled` — the common case) has no native switch beyond the boolean leaf the templates test. The mapping as written is inaccurate for most components a deployer meets.
findings.evidence: Design §2.2, §4 (a) example (`ingress` object with `x-zhi-component`); k8s-config-languages brief (Helm values practice, subchart scoping + `global`).
findings.suggested_fix: State the mapping as: subchart → `condition`; in-chart → a declared boolean leaf (`x-zhi-component: {name, enabledPointer: /ingress/enabled}`) that the component graph toggles; Kustomize → `Component`; Compose → `profiles`.

findings.section: §1.3 ("Every keystroke re-runs the Tier-0 chain") / §3.4 T0-b (Kyverno subprocess) / S7
findings.claim_or_choice: Per-keystroke re-run of the full Tier-0 chain including the Kyverno CLI subprocess, gated by S7 (<2 s warm) or the claim is dropped from copy.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: Even if S7 passes at 2 s, a 2-second debounce on every keystroke is not "inline" feedback; and a subprocess engine per keystroke on a consultant's VDI is the first thing that makes the UI feel broken. The stage-1 contract check (schema + values-CEL) is sub-millisecond and is what should run per keystroke; the rendered chain belongs on a longer debounce or on blur/save.
findings.evidence: Design §1.3, §3.3 stage 1, §10.1 S7; schema-validation-tech brief implication 1 ("validate whole tree per edit (sub-millisecond at values size)") and pain evidence on live per-keystroke validation cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify two cadences in §3.6: stage 0–1 per keystroke (in-process, ms); stages 2–18 on a 500 ms–1 s debounce with cancellation, with an explicit "revalidating…" state and the last full report kept visible. Add to S7 the Kyverno CLI cold-start time separately, and allow the Kyverno stage to run on save only when it exceeds a budget.

findings.section: §2.2 Workspace / §0 item 11 matrices / §13 fleet-and-evidence rejection
findings.claim_or_choice: A workspace is one GitOps repo; the compatibility matrix is package × environment within it.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: The supporter shipping release 4.7 into eleven customers has eleven customer-owned GitOps repos, i.e. eleven workspaces; the text matrix answers "which of my environments accept 4.7" per customer but never "which customers accept 4.7" — the question the supporter actually has on release day. The fleet proposal was rejected for its evidence baggage, but its one cheap idea (a tenant dimension) was dropped with it.
findings.evidence: Design §2.2, §0.11, §13 (fleet lost; "left the supporter with eleven customers looping by hand" is named as a minimalist flaw yet not fixed); persona brief §4 (Octopus Project × Environment × Tenant is "the most complete matrix model").
findings.suggested_fix: Let `zhi matrix --compat` accept multiple workspace paths/URLs (or a `fleet.yaml` listing them) and print package × (workspace/environment); no new storage, derived only. Phase 2 can add the tenant column to the UI matrix.

findings.section: §3.8 CLI / §5.2 / §12 Q13 (team without PR review, `allowDirectPush`)
findings.claim_or_choice: `zhi propose` opens a PR; `allowDirectPush` per environment is the only direct write; Blocking is refused on save in the UI.
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: For a one-person supporter at a small customer with no PR review and no bot, the local CLI is the only gate; the design does not say whether `zhi propose` refuses on Blocking, whether `allowDirectPush` still requires a clean report, or what audit trail a direct push leaves (the trailers exist only on proposal commits). Without that, the no-review team gets the least protection exactly where the bot is absent.
findings.evidence: Design §3.2 step 3 (UI refuses Blocking on save), §3.8, §5.2, §12 Q13; report §10.2 Q13.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify: `zhi propose` and any `allowDirectPush` write refuse on Blocking unless `--allow-blocking <finding-id>...` with a reason that is written into the commit trailer (`Zhi-Override:`), and direct pushes always carry the same trailers as proposals so post-merge feedback can correlate them.

findings.section: §7 v1 OpenShift data tier
findings.claim_or_choice: The data tier synthesises a UID-range placeholder Warning for namespaces the PR creates; SCC selection for existing namespaces waits for S11 (`sccmatching`).
findings.why_wrong_or_risky: For existing namespaces the snapshot already holds `openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range`/`supplemental-groups`, and the most common failure (chart hard-codes `runAsUser`/`fsGroup` outside the range while the SA is bound only to `restricted-v2`) is a direct arithmetic check that needs no `sccmatching` — the design leaves the higher-value existing-namespace case gated on the risky spike while shipping only the new-namespace placeholder.
findings.evidence: deployer brief OpenShift table rows "SCC selection" and "Namespace UID/GID/MCS pre-allocation" (annotations snapshot-able for existing namespaces; "#1 vendor-chart failure"); design §7 v1 paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the data tier: if the Pod's `runAsUser`/`fsGroup`/`supplementalGroups` are set and fall outside the namespace's annotated ranges, and the Pod's ServiceAccount has no `use` binding on an SCC with `RunAsAny`/`MustRunAs` covering it (RBAC layer), emit Blocking "restricted-v2 will reject" with `exactness: approximate`; keep full priority-ordered SCC selection on S11.

what_is_right: Git is the only write target and zhi never applies — the PR onto the folder Argo/Flux already watch is the one shape that survived every post-mortem (Monokle, Cyclops, Kubevious, Kubeapps, Weave GitOps); do not let any revision reintroduce an in-cluster component or a second source of truth (competitors brief Task C; report §8).

Build order CLI → bot → form with the form last in the *cut* list, not first: the bot in the push path is what gets validation in front of every PR author before anyone adopts a new editor (competitors brief; §0.2–0.3). Keep both lists distinct.

The developer↔deployer contract in standard shapes (`values.schema.json` 2020-12 enforced by Helm 4 itself, helm-cel-pattern CEL, Troubleshoot analyzers verbatim → Preflight Secret) so every artifact is useful without zhi at runtime (report §6.2; persona brief implications 1, 11).

The deployer-owned overlay at `.zhi/contracts/<package>/` — the consultant can annotate and add rules for Bitnami/vendor charts they cannot push to; this is the single feature that makes the consultant persona viable and the reviser must not fold it back into the chart (persona lens fatal flaw 3).

Fidelity in the Finding record (`tier`, `exactness`, `unobserved[]`, `wouldFailAt`, `side`), copy that never says "will apply", and T2 live dry-run as the calibration oracle in the test suite — the honest answer to Kyverno #5476 and KEP-5073 (report §5.3, §9 #8; fidelity brief).
`side ∈ {deployer, developer, platform}` on every finding — routing across the invisible border is the persona's core need; keep it even where lineage is weak.

Snapshot slices with redaction as a tested layer (golden fixtures), per-layer graceful degradation recorded in `manifest.json`, and `zhi snapshot rbac` producing a reviewable ClusterRole with a comment per rule — the right instincts for a bank's security review (cluster-state-import brief implications 1–2).

Comment- and marker-preserving yaml.v3 write-back of touched leaves only, with machine-owned pointers (Renovate, Image Updater, Kargo) read-only (report §9 #13; environments brief pain evidence on Image Updater formatting).
Server-side CEL visibility map so the browser never runs a second expression language — the Rancher Ember-vs-Jexl lesson applied correctly (persona brief pain evidence; engine-first §4.6).

Shallow plugin system: zero loadable plugins in v1, `Check`/`Resolver` as Go interfaces with one implementation each, exec adapters digest-pinned in `zhi.lock`, no PATH auto-detection, bot-mode allowlist — matches every brief's convergence and the audit's ~11k LOC of unused plumbing (report §7.3; audit lesson 6).
zhi-owned exit codes for every exec adapter, closing the Kyverno v1.12 exit-0-on-FAIL hole (devops brief; engine-first §4.7).
Severity mapping fixed in core with PolicyExceptions and `enforcementAction` honoured — deployers get the cluster's real posture, not a stricter shadow of it (report §9 #9).
Effective values with source layer per leaf and the stage-1 contract check before render so the deployer gets feedback even when the chart cannot render (report §3.1 class 16; contract-first §4.3).

OpenShift in the MVP as a data-tier profile with SCC emulation gated on a real spike — the right compromise between the persona and feasibility lenses; keep the UID placeholder Warning for new namespaces.

`zhi contract test` as a conformance table (`values → expected findings` against a fixture snapshot) — the mentoring loop for developers who start deploying, and the natural home for profile fixtures.
The spike sprint with numeric pass/fail criteria and the honest calendar (eight months for two people) — do not let the revision quietly re-inflate M1 beyond the ~15k LOC floor.
